GENERAL INFORMATION. 1.1 Purpose. This advisory circular (AC) supplements existing airworthiness approval guidance for attitude heading reference system (AHRS) articles approved under technical standard order (TSO)-C201, Attitude Heading Reference System, or later revisions. TSO-C201 includes performance standards for non-gimbaled attitude, heading, and turn and slip systems. Appendix A contains a list of acronyms. Appendix B explains where to obtain reference documents. Refer to the latest revision of following list of ACs to complete the aircraft type specific primary or stand-by flight instrument airworthiness certification process: a) AC 20-167, Airworthiness Approval of Enhanced Vision Systems, Synthetic Vision Systems, Combined Vision Systems, and Enhanced Flight Vision Systems; b) AC 23-8, Flight Test Guide for Certification of Part 23 Airplanes; c) AC 23-17, Systems and Equipment Guide for Certification of Part 23 Airplane and Airships; d) AC 23.1309-1, System Safety Analysis and Assessment for Part 23 Airplanes; e) AC 23.1311-1, Installation of Electronic Displays in Part 23 Airplanes; f) AC 25-7, Flight Test Guidance for Part 25 Airplanes; g) AC 25-11, Electronic Flight Deck Displays; h) AC 25.1302-1, Installed Systems and Equipment for Use by the Flightcrew; i) AC 25.1309-1, System Design and Analysis; j) AC 25.1322-1, Flightcrew Alerting; k) AC 25.1329-1, Approval of Flight Guidance Systems; l) AC 27-1, Certification of Normal Category Rotorcraft; and m) AC 29-2, Certification of Transport Category Rotorcraft. 1.2 Related CFR Regulations. Title 14 of the Code of Federal Regulations (14 CFR) a) Part 23, §§ 23.1301, .1303, .1309, .1311, .1321, .1322, and .1327. b) Part 25, §§ 25.1301, .1302, .1303, .1309, .1321, .1322, .1327, .1333, .1523 and Appendix D. c) Part 27, §§ 27.1301, .1303, .1309, .1321, .1322, .1327, and Appendix B. d) Part 29, §§ 29.1301, .1303, .1309, .1321, .1322, .1327, .1333, and Appendix B 1.3 Audience. This AC provides guidance for aircraft manufacturers, avionics manufacturers, installation shops, or other applicants seeking airworthiness approval under type certificate (TC), amended type certificate (ATC), supplemental type certificate (STC), or amended supplemental type certificate (ASTC) for TSO-C201 AHRS equipment. 1.4 Background. Manufacturers of attitude (pitch and roll), heading, turn and slip instruments have used TSO-C3, TSO-C4, TSO-C5, and TSO-C6 standards, dating back to 1958. More recently, AHRS based on micro-electro-mechanical systems (MEMS), ring-laser gyros (RLG), fiber optic gyros (FOG), and other technologies, are replacing conventional attitude and heading instruments to increase data performance reliability and accuracy. AHRS provides attitude and heading measurements with both static and dynamic accuracy comparable to traditional gimbaled systems. TSO-C201 does not cancel the older TSOs, but has been written for the non-gimbaled attitude and heading systems. When we published TSO-C201, many airworthiness approval policies existed for primary and stand-by flight instrumentation for each aircraft category type, as listed in Section 1.1. Although comprehensive, those policies do not address certain features included in TSO-C201 which require evaluation at installation. This AC's supplemental guidance addresses four specific areas: a) Aiding Sources; b) Degraded Mode; c) TSO-C201 Categorizations and Applications; and, d) Operational Considerations. 2. AHRS AIDING SOURCES. An AHRS aiding source is an internal or external system which provides additional sensor information to the core strap down attitude heading reference function. Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) and air data computer (ADC) aiding sources are commonly used to identify aircraft accelerations to reduce errors in the attitude function. Flux valves and magnetometers provide magnetic reference for heading functions, and numerous sources can be used for performance monitoring. Some aiding designs only supplement the AHRS functionality, and loss of aiding may only have limited effect on AHRS performance. On other designs, aiding may provide integral information where loss of the aiding source could lead to loss of AHRS functionality. 2.1 Internal Aiding Source Installations. Evaluate internal aiding sources as part of the overall article’s intended function evaluation. The internal aiding source should be qualified as part of the TSO-C201 design approval process. Ensure the aiding source provides the needed inputs with the appropriate accuracy, integrity, availability, and software level and electronic hardware design assurance for its intended use. For example, if the system was developed for a general aviation aircraft, but will be installed on a commuter aircraft, then the internal aiding source may need to be re-evaluated to ensure the appropriate compatibility with the aircraft’s design architecture and its usage. 2.2 External Aiding Source Installations. This paragraph applies to external aiding sources not qualified as part of the TSO-C201 article’s design approval. 2.2.1 External Aiding Source Performance. When the AHRS requires an external aiding source, ensure the aiding source installed in the aircraft provides the appropriate accuracy, integrity, availability, software level and electronic hardware design assurance. 2.2.2 External Aiding Source Annunciations. The applicant should determine how an external aiding source failure and annunciation affects AHRS performance. Conduct ground and flight testing as necessary to ensure appropriateness of the annunciation and pilot action. Any annunciations should be operationally relevant to minimize flightcrew workload; should be clear, unambiguous and timely; should only be indicated while the condition exists; should be consistently located in a specific area of the electronic display; and be located in the flightcrew’s primary field of view when immediate flightcrew awareness is required. If testing is not possible, provide an analysis to ensure the appropriate action occurs with degradation or failure of the external aiding source. For example, if the AHRS disables the attitude output or switches modes when the aiding source fails, as part of the §§23.1309, 25.1309, 27.1309, or 29.1309 safety analysis, ensure the AHRS acts per design when the aiding source is intentionally disabled. 2.3 GNSS Aiding. GNSS refers to all types of positioning satellites which provide autonomous geo-spatial positioning. Common GNSS systems include, but are not limited to, the navigation signal timing and ranging (NAVSTAR) global positioning system (GPS) (U.S.), globalnaya navigatsionnaya sputnikovaya sistema (GLONASS) (Russian) and Galileo (Europe). GNSS velocity data can be used to compute longitudinal accelerations to help eliminate errors. 2.3.1 GNSS Qualification: When interfacing the AHRS to an external GNSS, ensure the external GNSS provides the needed inputs with the appropriate accuracy, integrity, availability, and software and hardware design assurance. 2.3.1.1 When interfacing with an external GNSS, ensure the external GNSS is qualified to the standards of any revision of: a) TSO-C145d, Airborne Navigation Sensors Using the Global Positioning System Augmented by the Satellite Based Augmentation System; b) TSO-C146d, Stand-Alone Airborne Navigation Equipment Using the Global Positioning System Augmented by the Satellite Based Augmentation System; or c) TSO-C196b, Airborne Supplemental Navigation Sensors for Global Positioning System Equipment using Aircraft-Based Augmentation. 2.3.1.2 This AC does not address AHRS interface to TSO-C129a, Airborne Supplemental Navigation Equipment Using the Global Positioning System (GPS), since this TSO design standard may not provide sufficient availability in high interference environments. 2.3.2 GNSS Velocity Accuracy. If you use velocity accuracy from a GNSS position source, you should ensure the GNSS source data meets the minimum velocity accuracy requirement prescribed by the AHRS installation. GNSS position sources are not required to pass velocity accuracy tests to receive TSO authorization. One means to verify this performance is to ensure the GNSS source passes the velocity accuracy tests prescribed in AC 20-138D, Airworthiness Approval of Positioning and Navigation Systems or subsequent revisions. Typically, the GNSS source equipment manufacturer will accomplish these GNSS tests. 2.3.3 GNSS Faults. It is possible for some GNSS articles to output erroneous position and velocity data after the data is flagged invalid. Review the GNSS specifications to determine if this condition can occur, and if the AHRS detects the annunciated GNSS fault, the AHRS should cease using erroneous GNSS data. Analysis may be used as a means of compliance. 2.4 ADC Aiding. ADC information helps correct attitude pitch and bank angle errors. Ensure AHRS interfaces to an external ADC are qualified, such as any revision of TSO-C106, Air Data Computer, and provides the needed inputs with the appropriate accuracy, integrity, availability, and software and hardware design assurance. 2.5 Pitot Tube Airspeed Sensor Aiding. Pitot data information helps correct attitude pitch and bank angle error introduced by aircraft acceleration. It may directly interface with the AHRS. It is typically used for low velocity and non-complex velocity aircraft profiles. When interfacing the AHRS, ensure information is from a certified aircraft source (for example, TSO-C16, Electrically Heated Pitot and Pitot Static Tubes), and provides the needed inputs with the appropriate accuracy, integrity, availability, and software and hardware design assurance. For more complex velocities, the interface with an ADC may be necessary. Also see Rotorcraft Considerations in Section 5.5 2.6 Magnetic Aiding. When interfacing a magnetic sensor, ensure the sensor’s location is selected to avoid interference from the aircraft structure and systems. For interference associated with known aircraft magnetic anomalies, a compensator may be required to ensure accurate magnetic heading information. Ensure continuous operation of all heading instruments in all foreseeable operating conditions. 3. DEGRADED MODE. TSO-C201 provides allowances for an optional degraded mode to provide basic attitude performance when the AHRS has a partial failure or loses an aiding source. This mode is intended to allow an operator, even under instrument meteorological conditions (IMC), to maintain positive control of the aircraft. RTCA DO-334, Minimum Operational Performance Standards (MOPS) for Solid-State Strapdown Attitude and Heading Reference Systems (AHRS), indicates the degraded mode can support cruise flight, climbs, descents, holding, and instrument approaches. However, the degraded mode may not be acceptable for autopilot operation or certain flight procedures. Evaluate the degraded mode during the airworthiness certification to ensure suitability of the design and operation. Refer to the AHRS manufacturer’s installation manual for specific information regarding AHRS operating modes and equipment performance. 3.1 Degraded Mode Suitability. Determine if the degraded mode performance is acceptable for the intended aircraft and mode of operation in accordance with §§ 23.1301, 25.1301, 27.1301, or 29.1301. Degraded mode may be used on any aircraft type, for primary and secondary attitude sources; however, the TSO-C201 degraded mode is intended for smaller lower performance aircraft, such as part 23 and “non-appendix B” part 27 aircraft, which are typically certificated for one pilot and thus do not have two primary attitude systems installed. The degraded mode provides an alternative to a total loss of primary attitude in an aircraft with a single primary attitude system. In aircraft certificated for two pilot operations, use of the second primary attitude system is the preferred operating method when the first primary attitude system fails or degrades. Do not use degraded mode as a basis to reduce the required number of attitude instruments in an aircraft. If the AHRS installation manual requires flight envelope or time limitations for the degraded mode, insure those limitations are incorporated in the flight manual. The degraded mode is for abnormal conditions and should not be enabled while on the ground, either during initial system start-up or after engine start. 3.2 Degraded Mode Testing. There are two types of degraded mode triggers in AHRS equipment. One can be evaluated in-flight and the other cannot. 3.2.1 For initial AHRS installations, where the degraded mode can be disabled in-flight, such as circuit breaker pull, then the degraded mode should be evaluated through flight testing. 3.2.2 For initial AHRS installations, where the degraded mode cannot be evaluated in-flight, such as accelerometer degradation, then the applicant may use analysis or simulation. Testing should include pilot workload, acceptability of degraded mode through normal instrument flight rules (IFR) maneuvers, including climbs, descents, standard rate turns, and instrument approaches. Testing should also evaluate any effects on the flightcrew’s ability to control the aircraft in flight. 3.2.3 Follow-on installations should demonstrate degraded mode performance for unique aircraft flight envelopes or operating conditions. Applicants using analysis to comply with §§23.1309, 25.1309, 27.1309, 29.1309 and 25.1523 and appendix D to part25 should ensure the degraded mode will safely perform its intended function and will not significantly affect pilot workload or aircraft operation. This analysis should also take into account any effects on the flightcrew’s ability to control the aircraft in flight. In either case, the airplane/rotorcraft flight manual supplement (A/RFMS) should include the degraded mode performance characteristics and limitations. 3.3 Other System Interfaces. The degraded mode performance was defined to support primary attitude, heading, turn rate, and slip-skid indications. Evaluate the suitability of the degraded mode performance for other applications, as it may not be sufficient for higher performance applications, such as an autopilot, head-up display (HUD), or a synthetic vision system (SVS) display. If the analysis shows the degraded mode is not sufficient for other aircraft applications, ensure the degraded mode does not drive those particular aircraft applications. 3.4 Operating Instructions. Ensure the appropriate A/RFMS or applicable operating instructions are updated with a description of the degraded mode, the annunciations provided in degraded mode, and instructions for operating the aircraft. The operating instructions should also indicate which system applications will be lost (e.g., autopilot) and the limitations on types of maneuvers or operations which can be accomplished in degraded mode. 4. TSO-C201 CATEGORIZATIONS AND APPLICATIONS. AHRS, as a minimum, provides attitude information to pilots and/or aircraft. It may also provide heading, turn and slip and other information including acceleration, vertical speed, angular rates, lateral velocity, track data and position. TSO-C201 AHRS articles will typically be identified with a six digit category string. The first two letters define the attitude accuracy, the third and fourth letters define the heading accuracy and availability, and the fifth and sixth letters define the turn and slip capability. For example, the category string A4H4T3 denotes a dynamic attitude accuracy of 2.5º, dynamic heading accuracy of 6^° with magnetic slaving, and turn rate and slip information is provided. It is possible the AHRS will have different category strings for different modes of operation. Refer to RTCA DO-334, section 2.2 for descriptions of the attitude, heading and turn and slip categories. 4.1 Attitude Category and Application. The attitude categories, A1 through A5, primarily pertain to the accuracy of the AHRS attitude output. All five categories are suitable to drive basic attitude indicators. Some applications, such as HUD and integration of autopilot, may require the higher accuracy categories. Refer to the interfacing systems attitude performance and airworthiness requirements and ensure your AHRS installation meets those requirements. 4.2 Heading Category and Application. There are eleven (11) potential heading categories for TSO-C201 articles, all of which articulate the accuracy of the heading information and its source. The H1 system uses a non-magnetic heading determination (e.g., a gyrocompassing system), the H2 through H5 systems are magnetically slaved (e.g., to a flux valve or magnetometer), and the H6 through H11 categories operate in directional gyro (DG) mode. All heading categories are suitable to drive basic heading indicators; however, categories H10 and H11 are for short-term use when magnetic anomalies exist. Some applications, such as enhanced flight vision systems (EFVS) and integration of the flight management system (FMS) may require higher accuracy categories. Refer to the interfacing systems heading performance and airworthiness requirements and ensure your AHRS installation meets those requirements. 4.3 Turn and Slip Category Application. The seven (7) turn and slip categories, T1 through T7 relate to the availability of turn, bank angle, slip and skid information. Refer to the interfacing systems of turn, bank angle, slip and skid performance and airworthiness requirements and ensure your installation meets those requirements. 4.4 Other AHRS Information for Other Applications. AHRS articles can also provide other features such as acceleration, vertical velocity, angular rates, magnetic wind direction, ground speed, magnetic track angle, and velocity. TSO-C201 does not provide performance requirements for this data, so ensure the AHRS data is appropriate for the intended applications. 4 BACKGROUND. 4.1 Airborne Doppler Weather Radar Systems with Forward-Looking Windshear Detection. The forward-looking windshear detection function is incorporated into TSO-C63e. This AC incorporates and clarifies appropriate airworthiness guidance and eliminates errata from System Level Requirements (SLR) 10.2 “Airborne Short and Long Range Windshear Predictive Systems (Forward-Looking Windshear Systems) Interim Certification Requirements, Revision 10.2.” SLR 10.2 is no longer applicable for systems that comply with TSO-C63e or later. 4.2 Airborne Doppler Weather Radar Systems with Forward-Looking Turbulence Detection. Prior to February 2012, the FAA used design standards developed by the Airborne Turbulence Detection Systems (ATDS) Working Group and airworthiness requirements documented in issue papers to certify forward looking turbulence detection radars. The FAA published TSO-C63d in February 2012, incorporating the ATDS Working Group design requirements. With the release of TSO-C63e, the turbulence detection function continues to be included in the TSO. This AC incorporates the remaining airworthiness guidance from issue papers into formally published FAA guidance. 2 AUDIENCE. We wrote this AC for aircraft manufacturers, laser equipment manufacturers, installation shops, and other applicants seeking FAA airworthiness approval of invisible spectrum laser equipment installations on part 23, 25, 27, and 29 aircraft. The airworthiness approval can occur under a type certificate (TC), supplemental type certificate (STC), amended type certificate (ATC), amended supplemental type certificate (ASTC) or data approval for major alteration. This AC also provides guidance to FAA personnel involved in a TC, STC, ATC, ASTC, or data approval for major alterations that install invisible spectrum laser equipment. 9 TEST AND EVALUATION. This section provides guidance for testing radar systems on aircraft. Follow the guidance in section 9.1 for weather and ground mapping radar. Follow the guidance in section 9.2 if your radar system includes a forward-looking windshear detection function. Follow the guidance in section 9.3 if your radar system includes turbulence detection or atmospheric threat awareness functions. Testing of all radar systems should ensure:  The radar antenna and radome combination function correctly; The radar display and alert prioritization functions correctly and the alerts, alert inhibits, annunciations, and controls function correctly;  The fault detection functionality works properly;  The human factors interface is acceptable;  The radar does not adversely interfere with other systems; and  Other systems do not adversely interfere with the radar. 9.1 Weather Radar. Accomplish flight test of the weather and ground mapping pulsed radar functions in accordance with the latest revision of the following ACs for parts 23, 25, 27, and 29 aircraft: 9.1.1 AC 23-8, Flight Test Guide for Certification of Part 23 Airplanes, Chapter 5, paragraph 1.b (10). 9.1.2 AC 25-7, Flight Test Guide for Certification of Transport Category Airplanes, Chapter 6, section 1, paragraph 170.c(8). 9.1.3 AC 27-1, Change 3, Certification of Normal Category Rotorcraft Chapter 3, AC 27 MG 1, paragraph b (10). 9.1.4 AC 29-2, Change 3, Certification of Transport Category Rotorcraft Chapter 3, AC 29 MG 1, paragraph b (10). 9.2 Forward-Looking Windshear Detection. Follow the TSO instructions to verify performance of the forward-looking windshear function. Installation testing of the forward-looking windshear function often relies on general weather radar functional testing as described in paragraphs 9.1.1 and 9.1.2 of this AC and integration testing versus dedicated forward-looking windshear flight testing. 9.2.1 Penetration Flight Evaluation. Penetration flights will typically be accomplished by the radar manufacturer as part of the TSO authorization. If penetration data and analysis are available and you determine they are applicable, then you do not need to conduct penetration flight tests. Previously approved test data generated during the TSO authorization or previous certification effort is acceptable. If forward-looking windshear capability was not previously demonstrated, then verify the detection capability of the forward-looking windshear system by flying in areas of convective activity that can be verified by in-situ measurements, appropriate ground-based radar systems, or the equivalent. Note: Flying in or near storm cells can be extremely hazardous. Flight crews should exercise good judgment for safe flight based on knowledge of their own abilities and of the capability of the aircraft when considering approaching or penetrating any storm cell or turbulent area. 9.2.2 Clutter Suppression Flight Test. Evaluate the system’s ability to reject spurious conditions (e.g., clutter suppression, bi/multi-static signal interference, range ambiguous returns, and radome effects). The flight tests may be conducted under visual meteorological conditions. Conduct this evaluation at one or more airports with the following characteristics: 9.2.2.1 Expressways and high-volume surface streets within approximately 1 nm of the runway. 9.2.2.2 Nearby taxiing aircraft. 9.2.2.3 Concentrated urban clutter. The clutter should occupy a minimum area of approximately 1 nm surrounding the airport. 9.3 Turbulence Detection or Atmospheric Threat Awareness. Follow the TSO installation instructions to verify performance of turbulence detection or atmospheric threat awareness functions. Atmospheric threat awareness functions could include, but are not limited to, hail and lightning indication. Installation testing of these functions often relies on general weather radar functional testing as described in paragraphs 9.1.1 and 9.1.2 of this AC and integration testing versus dedicated flight testing. You should attempt to evaluate the performance of these functions against operationally significant weather when weather is reasonably available and you can do so without placing the aircraft in the hazardous weather. This performance evaluation should ensure the depiction of turbulence or weather hazard is consistent with actual weather phenomenon. Data from the radar manufacturer may be used to supplement or replace additional flight testing if the data is determined to be applicable. ## 结论先行

| 判断项 | 结论 |
|---|---|
| 用同一份多型号批准把 Part 23 固定翼与 Part 27 旋翼机合并成一张清单 | 本次检索到的资料**没有**任何关于“多型号批准/型号清单如何编排”的条款，因此无法据资料认定可以合并；但资料明确显示，法规与指导文件是**按航空器类别（Part 23 / Part 25 / Part 27 / Part 29）分别列项、分别引用**的 |
| “指导文件覆盖四类航空器”因而前视风切变功能也覆盖四类 | **不成立为一般结论**。覆盖 Part 23、25、27、29 四类的表述出现在 §9.1“气象雷达与地面测绘功能飞行试验”；而 §9.2“前视风切变探测”只引用 §9.1.1（Part 23）与 §9.1.2（Part 25），**未引用** §9.1.3（Part 27）与 §9.1.4（Part 29） |

---

## 一、批准清单的组织方式

**1. 资料未给出多型号批准的编排规则。** 检索到的内容中没有关于“多型号改装批准”“型号清单（清单式批准）”应如何组织、能否跨类别合并的条文。因此“用同一份批准同时覆盖 Part 23 与 Part 27”这一做法，**无法从现有资料得到支持或否定**。

**2. 可支持的事实：指导体系按类别分列，而非合并列项。**
- AC 20-184 附录 B 的“相关法规与文件”表中，Part 23（Airworthiness Standards: Normal Utility, Acrobatic, and Commuter Category Airplanes）与 Part 27（Airworthiness Standards: Normal Category Rotorcraft）是**两个独立条目**，其后的咨询通告也按 Part 分别列出（AC 23-17C 对应 Part 23，AC 27-1B 对应 Part 27）<kb doc="AC_20-184.pdf" chunk_id="509241d7-43ef-4186-8952-53fcd3cf8c04" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" /><kb doc="AC_20-184.pdf" chunk_id="c4615217-bbe5-46d2-b9d6-17f2c62102f6" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" />。
- AC 20-182A 附录 B 同样把 AC 23-8（Part 23）、AC 25-7（Part 25）、AC 27-1（Part 27）、AC 29-2（Part 29）作为**四个独立文件**列出，并注明所引 AC 与 TSO 均指现行版本<kb doc="AC_20-182A.pdf" chunk_id="1ff290bb-d30f-4e37-a185-22241e2c8129" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" />。

![table p19](http://localhost:8080/api/v1/ingestion/jobs/9b93535e939046d88b3e1f6f97c3f2a8/assets/5e24440b80754c81134a)

**3. 由此可作的推论（标注为推论，非文件要求）：** 清单若要成立，至少需要按航空器类别区分**认证基础**与**对应类别的指导文件**，不能把 Part 23 与 Part 27 混为一条不分类别的条目；“雷达型号相同、基线数据相同”本身不是资料中任何清单编排规则的依据。

---

## 二、前视风切变指导的适用范围

**1. 功能层面的依据是 TSO-C63e，而非按机型划分。** 前视风切变探测功能已纳入 TSO-C63e；该 AC 整合并澄清相应适航指导，并消除 SLR 10.2 的勘误；对符合 TSO-C63e 或其后版本的系统，SLR 10.2 不再适用<kb doc="AC_20-182A.pdf" chunk_id="a90a1163-1f39-4115-9eac-3ef761cc6f2d" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" />。

**2. 安装测试层面：§9.1 覆盖四类，§9.2 只引用 Part 23 与 Part 25。**

| 条款 | 内容 | 引用的按类别文件 |
|---|---|---|
| §9.1（气象雷达/地面测绘） | 按下列 AC 最新版对 **parts 23, 25, 27, and 29** 航空器实施飞行试验 | 9.1.1 AC 23-8 第5章 1.b(10)；9.1.2 AC 25-7 第6章第1节 170.c(8)；9.1.3 AC 27-1 Change 3 第3章 AC 27 MG 1 b(10)；9.1.4 AC 29-2 Change 3 第3章 AC 29 MG 1 b(10) <kb doc="AC_20-182A.pdf" chunk_id="ffeb9ba1-f0f8-4bd4-8ac2-7491229dfc8b" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" /> |
| §9.2（前视风切变探测） | 按 TSO 说明验证前视风切变功能性能；安装测试**often relies on** §9.1.1 与 §9.1.2 所述的一般气象雷达功能测试，以及集成测试（相对于专门的风切变飞行试验） | 仅 **9.1.1、9.1.2**（Part 23、Part 25）；未引用 9.1.3、9.1.4 <kb doc="AC_20-182A.pdf" chunk_id="6af45402-50ba-4ae0-80db-9c1bb1907f16" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" /> |

**3. 因此，“指导文件覆盖四类航空器”这一理由在资料中成立的范围是 §9.1 的气象雷达/地面测绘功能试验；“前视风切变”专用条款中的试验依托对象只指向 Part 23 与 Part 25 的飞行试验指南。** 资料中不存在“前视风切变安装测试按 AC 27-1 / AC 29-2 执行”的表述。这属于对检索文本引用范围的如实陈述，并非断言原文否定旋翼机适用。

**4. 穿透飞行数据可复用，但有条件。** 穿透飞行通常由雷达制造商在 TSO 授权过程中完成；若穿透数据与分析可用且申请人判定其适用，则无需再做穿透飞行试验，此前在 TSO 授权或以往取证中产生的数据可接受；若前视风切变能力此前未经演示，则须通过在可被实测、地面雷达或等效手段核实的对流活动区域飞行来验证探测能力<kb doc="AC_20-182A.pdf" chunk_id="6af45402-50ba-4ae0-80db-9c1bb1907f16" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" />。这支持“型号级数据可复用”，但不等于“安装批准可跨类别通用”。

**5. 杂波抑制飞行试验**需在具备下列特征的机场评估系统抑制虚警的能力（可在目视气象条件下进行）：跑道约 1 nm 内的高速公路与高流量地面道路；附近滑行中的航空器；机场周边约至少 1 nm 范围的密集城市杂波<kb doc="AC_20-182A.pdf" chunk_id="82fbc2af-fda2-4c40-942e-1f3574248bac" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" />。

---

## 三、“型号与基线数据相同”能推到哪一步

- 能推到：TSO 层面的功能标准统一（TSO-C63e 含前视风切变），以及 §9.2.1 所述穿透数据的条件性复用<kb doc="AC_20-182A.pdf" chunk_id="a90a1163-1f39-4115-9eac-3ef761cc6f2d" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" /><kb doc="AC_20-182A.pdf" chunk_id="6af45402-50ba-4ae0-80db-9c1bb1907f16" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" />。
- 不能推到：安装批准与按类别试验的免除。类别对应的试验指南在资料中是分列的，且 §9.2 的引用范围窄于 §9.1<kb doc="AC_20-182A.pdf" chunk_id="ffeb9ba1-f0f8-4bd4-8ac2-7491229dfc8b" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" /><kb doc="AC_20-182A.pdf" chunk_id="6af45402-50ba-4ae0-80db-9c1bb1907f16" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" />。

---

## 四、当前资料无法确定的事项

1. 多型号改装批准（清单式批准）的编排规则、能否跨 Part 23/Part 27 合并——检索内容中无相关条款。
2. 前视风切变功能在 Part 27 旋翼机上的专用安装试验要求——§9.2 未给出对应类别引用，资料中也无其他条款补足。
3. AC 20-182A 自身的适用机型范围声明（本次检索未包含其“适用范围/目的”正文条款）。

---

## 补充参考（非上述判断的直接依据）

AC 20-182A §11 要求将下列内容纳入持续适航文件（ICA）：雷达系统与天线罩的维护说明、雷达与飞机的接口描述、维持天线罩与天线性能的校准说明、雷达系统与天线罩的检查间隔、雷达运行的危害区域；并指出天线罩即使微小修理也应恢复到气象雷达工作所需的最低性能，可参考 AC 43-14 与 RTCA/DO-213A<kb doc="AC_20-182A.pdf" chunk_id="e791bb99-d55d-4ec0-bb7d-f6656dbde9df" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" />。该项内容按安装编制，资料中未给出“型号相同即可通用”的表述。

1. GENERAL INFORMATION.

1.1 Purpose. This advisory circular (AC) supplements existing airworthiness approval guidance for attitude heading reference system (AHRS) articles approved under technical standard order (TSO)-C201, Attitude Heading Reference System, or later revisions. TSO-C201 includes performance standards for non-gimbaled attitude, heading, and turn and slip systems. Appendix A contains a list of acronyms. Appendix B explains where to obtain reference documents. Refer to the latest revision of following list of ACs to complete the aircraft type specific primary or stand-by flight instrument airworthiness certification process:

a)	 AC 20-167, Airworthiness Approval of Enhanced Vision Systems, Synthetic Vision Systems, Combined Vision Systems, and Enhanced Flight Vision Systems;

b) AC 23-8, Flight Test Guide for Certification of Part 23 Airplanes;

c) AC 23-17, Systems and Equipment Guide for Certification of Part 23 Airplane and Airships;

d) AC 23.1309-1, System Safety Analysis and Assessment for Part 23 Airplanes;

e) AC 23.1311-1, Installation of Electronic Displays in Part 23 Airplanes;

f) AC 25-7, Flight Test Guidance for Part 25 Airplanes;

g) AC 25-11, Electronic Flight Deck Displays;

h) AC 25.1302-1, Installed Systems and Equipment for Use by the Flightcrew;

i) AC 25.1309-1, System Design and Analysis;

j) AC 25.1322-1, Flightcrew Alerting;

k) AC 25.1329-1, Approval of Flight Guidance Systems;

l) AC 27-1, Certification of Normal Category Rotorcraft; and

m) AC 29-2, Certification of Transport Category Rotorcraft.

1.2 Related CFR Regulations. Title 14 of the Code of Federal Regulations (14 CFR)

a)	 Part 23, §§ 23.1301, .1303, .1309, .1311, .1321, .1322, and .1327.

b)	 Part 25, §§ 25.1301, .1302, .1303, .1309, .1321, .1322, .1327, .1333, .1523 and Appendix D.

c)	 Part 27, §§ 27.1301, .1303, .1309, .1321, .1322, .1327, and Appendix B.

d)	 Part 29, §§ 29.1301, .1303, .1309, .1321, .1322, .1327, .1333, and Appendix B

1.3 Audience. This AC provides guidance for aircraft manufacturers, avionics manufacturers, installation shops, or other applicants seeking airworthiness approval under type certificate (TC), amended type certificate (ATC), supplemental type certificate (STC), or amended supplemental type certificate (ASTC) for TSO-C201 AHRS equipment.

1.4 Background. Manufacturers of attitude (pitch and roll), heading, turn and slip instruments have used TSO-C3, TSO-C4, TSO-C5, and TSO-C6 standards, dating back to 1958. More recently, AHRS based on micro-electro-mechanical systems (MEMS), ring-laser gyros (RLG), fiber optic gyros (FOG), and other technologies, are replacing conventional attitude and heading instruments to increase data performance reliability and accuracy. AHRS provides attitude and heading measurements with both static and dynamic accuracy comparable to traditional gimbaled systems. TSO-C201 does not cancel the older TSOs, but has been written for the non-gimbaled attitude and heading systems. When we published TSO-C201, many airworthiness approval policies existed for primary and stand-by flight instrumentation for each aircraft category type, as listed in Section 1.1. Although comprehensive, those policies do not address certain features included in TSO-C201 which require evaluation at installation. This AC's supplemental guidance addresses four specific areas:

a)	 Aiding Sources;

b)	 Degraded Mode;

c)	 TSO-C201 Categorizations and Applications; and,

d)	 Operational Considerations.

2. AHRS AIDING SOURCES. An AHRS aiding source is an internal or external system which provides additional sensor information to the core strap down attitude heading reference function. Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) and air data computer (ADC) aiding sources are commonly used to identify aircraft accelerations to reduce errors in the attitude function. Flux valves and magnetometers provide magnetic reference for heading functions, and numerous sources can be used for performance monitoring. Some aiding designs only supplement the AHRS functionality, and loss of aiding may only have limited effect on AHRS performance. On other designs, aiding may provide integral information where loss of the aiding source could lead to loss of AHRS functionality.

2.1 Internal Aiding Source Installations. Evaluate internal aiding sources as part of the overall article’s intended function evaluation. The internal aiding source should be qualified as part of the TSO-C201 design approval process. Ensure the aiding source provides the needed inputs with the appropriate accuracy, integrity, availability, and software level and electronic hardware design

assurance for its intended use. For example, if the system was developed for a general aviation aircraft, but will be installed on a commuter aircraft, then the internal aiding source may need to be re-evaluated to ensure the appropriate compatibility with the aircraft’s design architecture and its usage.

2.2 External Aiding Source Installations. This paragraph applies to external aiding sources not qualified as part of the TSO-C201 article’s design approval.

2.2.1 External Aiding Source Performance. When the AHRS requires an external aiding source, ensure the aiding source installed in the aircraft provides the appropriate accuracy, integrity, availability, software level and electronic hardware design assurance.

2.2.2 External Aiding Source Annunciations. The applicant should determine how an external aiding source failure and annunciation affects AHRS performance. Conduct ground and flight testing as necessary to ensure appropriateness of the annunciation and pilot action. Any annunciations should be operationally relevant to minimize flightcrew workload; should be clear, unambiguous and timely; should only be indicated while the condition exists; should be consistently located in a specific area of the electronic display; and be located in the flightcrew’s primary field of view when immediate flightcrew awareness is required. If testing is not possible, provide an analysis to ensure the appropriate action occurs with degradation or failure of the external aiding source. For example, if the AHRS disables the attitude output or switches modes when the aiding source fails, as part of the §§23.1309, 25.1309, 27.1309, or 29.1309 safety analysis, ensure the AHRS acts per design when the aiding source is intentionally disabled.

2.3 GNSS Aiding. GNSS refers to all types of positioning satellites which provide autonomous geo-spatial positioning. Common GNSS systems include, but are not limited to, the navigation signal timing and ranging (NAVSTAR) global positioning system (GPS) (U.S.), globalnaya navigatsionnaya sputnikovaya sistema (GLONASS) (Russian) and Galileo (Europe). GNSS velocity data can be used to compute longitudinal accelerations to help eliminate errors.

2.3.1 GNSS Qualification: When interfacing the AHRS to an external GNSS, ensure the external GNSS provides the needed inputs with the appropriate accuracy, integrity, availability, and software and hardware design assurance.

2.3.1.1 When interfacing with an external GNSS, ensure the external GNSS is qualified to the standards of any revision of:

a) TSO-C145d, Airborne Navigation Sensors Using the Global Positioning System Augmented by the Satellite Based Augmentation System;

b) TSO-C146d, Stand-Alone Airborne Navigation Equipment Using the Global Positioning System Augmented by the Satellite Based Augmentation System; or

c) TSO-C196b, Airborne Supplemental Navigation Sensors for Global Positioning System Equipment using Aircraft-Based Augmentation.

2.3.1.2 This AC does not address AHRS interface to TSO-C129a, Airborne Supplemental Navigation Equipment Using the Global Positioning System (GPS), since this TSO design standard may not provide sufficient availability in high interference environments.

2.3.2 GNSS Velocity Accuracy. If you use velocity accuracy from a GNSS position source, you should ensure the GNSS source data meets the minimum velocity accuracy requirement prescribed by the AHRS installation. GNSS position sources are not required to pass velocity accuracy tests to receive TSO authorization. One means to verify this performance is to ensure the GNSS source passes the velocity accuracy tests prescribed in AC 20-138D, Airworthiness Approval of Positioning and Navigation Systems or subsequent revisions. Typically, the GNSS source equipment manufacturer will accomplish these GNSS tests.

2.3.3 GNSS Faults. It is possible for some GNSS articles to output erroneous position and velocity data after the data is flagged invalid. Review the GNSS specifications to determine if this condition can occur, and if the AHRS detects the annunciated GNSS fault, the AHRS should cease using erroneous GNSS data. Analysis may be used as a means of compliance.

2.4 ADC Aiding. ADC information helps correct attitude pitch and bank angle errors. Ensure AHRS interfaces to an external ADC are qualified, such as any revision of TSO-C106, Air Data Computer, and provides the needed inputs with the appropriate accuracy, integrity, availability, and software and hardware design assurance.

2.5 Pitot Tube Airspeed Sensor Aiding. Pitot data information helps correct attitude pitch and bank angle error introduced by aircraft acceleration. It may directly interface with the AHRS. It is typically used for low velocity and non-complex velocity aircraft profiles. When interfacing the AHRS, ensure information is from a certified aircraft source (for example, TSO-C16, Electrically Heated Pitot and Pitot Static Tubes), and provides the needed inputs with the appropriate accuracy, integrity, availability, and software and hardware design assurance. For more complex velocities, the interface with an ADC may be necessary. Also see Rotorcraft Considerations in Section 5.5

2.6 Magnetic Aiding. When interfacing a magnetic sensor, ensure the sensor’s location is selected to avoid interference from the aircraft structure and systems. For interference associated with known aircraft magnetic anomalies, a compensator may be required to ensure accurate magnetic heading information. Ensure continuous operation of all heading instruments in all foreseeable operating conditions.

3. DEGRADED MODE. TSO-C201 provides allowances for an optional degraded mode to provide basic attitude performance when the AHRS has a partial failure or loses an aiding source. This mode is intended to allow an operator, even under instrument meteorological conditions (IMC), to maintain positive control of the aircraft. RTCA DO-334, Minimum Operational Performance Standards (MOPS) for Solid-State Strapdown Attitude and Heading Reference Systems (AHRS), indicates the degraded mode can support cruise flight, climbs, descents, holding, and instrument approaches. However, the degraded mode may not be acceptable for autopilot operation or certain flight procedures. Evaluate the degraded mode during the airworthiness certification to ensure suitability of the design and operation. Refer to the AHRS manufacturer’s installation manual for specific information regarding AHRS operating modes and equipment performance.

3.1 Degraded Mode Suitability. Determine if the degraded mode performance is acceptable for the intended aircraft and mode of operation in accordance with §§ 23.1301, 25.1301, 27.1301, or 29.1301. Degraded mode may be used on any aircraft type, for primary and secondary attitude sources; however, the TSO-C201 degraded mode is intended for smaller lower performance aircraft, such as part 23 and “non-appendix B” part 27 aircraft, which are typically certificated for one pilot and thus do not have two primary attitude systems installed. The degraded mode provides an alternative to a total loss of primary attitude in an aircraft with a single primary attitude system. In aircraft certificated for two pilot operations, use of the second primary attitude system is the preferred operating method when the first primary attitude system fails or degrades. Do not use degraded mode as a basis to reduce the required number of attitude instruments in an aircraft. If the AHRS installation manual requires flight envelope or time limitations for the degraded mode, insure those limitations are incorporated in the flight manual. The degraded mode is for abnormal conditions and should not be enabled while on the ground, either during initial system start-up or after engine start.

3.2 Degraded Mode Testing. There are two types of degraded mode triggers in AHRS equipment. One can be evaluated in-flight and the other cannot.

3.2.1 For initial AHRS installations, where the degraded mode can be disabled in-flight, such as circuit breaker pull, then the degraded mode should be evaluated through flight testing.

3.2.2 For initial AHRS installations, where the degraded mode cannot be evaluated in-flight, such as accelerometer degradation, then the applicant may use analysis or simulation. Testing should include pilot workload, acceptability of degraded mode through normal instrument flight rules (IFR) maneuvers, including climbs, descents, standard rate turns, and instrument approaches. Testing should also evaluate any effects on the flightcrew’s ability to control the aircraft in flight.

3.2.3 Follow-on installations should demonstrate degraded mode performance for unique aircraft flight envelopes or operating conditions. Applicants using analysis to comply with §§23.1309, 25.1309, 27.1309, 29.1309 and 25.1523 and appendix D to part25 should ensure the degraded mode will safely perform its intended function and will not significantly affect pilot workload or aircraft operation. This analysis should also take into account any effects on the flightcrew’s ability to control the aircraft in flight. In either case, the airplane/rotorcraft flight manual supplement (A/RFMS) should include the degraded mode performance characteristics and limitations.

3.3 Other System Interfaces. The degraded mode performance was defined to support primary attitude, heading, turn rate, and slip-skid indications. Evaluate the suitability of the degraded mode performance for other applications, as it may not be sufficient for higher performance applications, such as an autopilot, head-up display (HUD), or a synthetic vision system (SVS) display. If the analysis shows the degraded mode is not sufficient for other aircraft applications, ensure the degraded mode does not drive those particular aircraft applications.

3.4 Operating Instructions. Ensure the appropriate A/RFMS or applicable operating instructions are updated with a description of the degraded mode, the annunciations provided in degraded mode, and instructions for operating the aircraft. The operating instructions should also indicate which system applications will be lost (e.g., autopilot) and the limitations on types of maneuvers or operations which can be accomplished in degraded mode.

4. TSO-C201 CATEGORIZATIONS AND APPLICATIONS. AHRS, as a minimum, provides attitude information to pilots and/or aircraft. It may also provide heading, turn and slip and other information including acceleration, vertical speed, angular rates, lateral velocity, track data and position. TSO-C201 AHRS articles will typically be identified with a six digit category string. The first two letters define the attitude accuracy, the third and fourth letters define the heading accuracy and availability, and the fifth and sixth letters define the turn and slip capability. For example, the category string A4H4T3 denotes a dynamic attitude accuracy of 2.5º, dynamic heading accuracy of 6^° with magnetic slaving, and turn rate and slip information is provided. It is possible the AHRS will

have different category strings for different modes of operation. Refer to RTCA DO-334, section 2.2 for descriptions of the attitude, heading and turn and slip categories.

4.1 Attitude Category and Application. The attitude categories, A1 through A5, primarily pertain to the accuracy of the AHRS attitude output. All five categories are suitable to drive basic attitude indicators. Some applications, such as HUD and integration of autopilot, may require the higher accuracy categories. Refer to the interfacing systems attitude performance and airworthiness requirements and ensure your AHRS installation meets those requirements.

4.2 Heading Category and Application. There are eleven (11) potential heading categories for TSO-C201 articles, all of which articulate the accuracy of the heading information and its source. The H1 system uses a non-magnetic heading determination (e.g., a gyrocompassing system), the H2 through H5 systems are magnetically slaved (e.g., to a flux valve or magnetometer), and the H6 through H11 categories operate in directional gyro (DG) mode. All heading categories are suitable to drive basic heading indicators; however, categories H10 and H11 are for short-term use when magnetic anomalies exist. Some applications, such as enhanced flight vision systems (EFVS) and integration of the flight management system (FMS) may require higher accuracy categories. Refer to the interfacing systems heading performance and airworthiness requirements and ensure your AHRS installation meets those requirements.

4.3 Turn and Slip Category Application. The seven (7) turn and slip categories, T1 through T7 relate to the availability of turn, bank angle, slip and skid information. Refer to the interfacing systems of turn, bank angle, slip and skid performance and airworthiness requirements and ensure your installation meets those requirements.

4.4 Other AHRS Information for Other Applications. AHRS articles can also provide other features such as acceleration, vertical velocity, angular rates, magnetic wind direction, ground speed, magnetic track angle, and velocity. TSO-C201 does not provide performance requirements for this data, so ensure the AHRS data is appropriate for the intended applications.

4 BACKGROUND.

4.1 Airborne Doppler Weather Radar Systems with Forward-Looking Windshear Detection.

The forward-looking windshear detection function is incorporated into TSO-C63e. This AC incorporates and clarifies appropriate airworthiness guidance and eliminates errata from System Level Requirements (SLR) 10.2 “Airborne Short and Long Range Windshear Predictive Systems (Forward-Looking Windshear Systems) Interim Certification Requirements, Revision 10.2.” SLR 10.2 is no longer applicable for systems that comply with TSO-C63e or later.

4.2 Airborne Doppler Weather Radar Systems with Forward-Looking Turbulence Detection.

Prior to February 2012, the FAA used design standards developed by the Airborne Turbulence Detection Systems (ATDS) Working Group and airworthiness requirements documented in issue papers to certify forward looking turbulence detection radars. The FAA published TSO-C63d in February 2012, incorporating the ATDS Working Group design requirements. With the release of TSO-C63e, the turbulence detection function continues to be included in the TSO. This AC incorporates the remaining airworthiness guidance from issue papers into formally published FAA guidance.

9 TEST AND EVALUATION.

This section provides guidance for testing radar systems on aircraft. Follow the guidance in section 9.1 for weather and ground mapping radar. Follow the guidance in section 9.2 if your radar system includes a forward-looking windshear detection function. Follow the guidance in section 9.3 if your radar system includes turbulence detection or atmospheric threat awareness functions. Testing of all radar systems should ensure:

 The radar antenna and radome combination function correctly;

The radar display and alert prioritization functions correctly and the alerts, alert inhibits, annunciations, and controls function correctly;

 The fault detection functionality works properly;

 The human factors interface is acceptable;

 The radar does not adversely interfere with other systems; and

 Other systems do not adversely interfere with the radar.

9.1 Weather Radar.

Accomplish flight test of the weather and ground mapping pulsed radar functions in accordance with the latest revision of the following ACs for parts 23, 25, 27, and 29 aircraft:

9.1.1 AC 23-8, Flight Test Guide for Certification of Part 23 Airplanes, Chapter 5, paragraph 1.b (10).

9.1.2 AC 25-7, Flight Test Guide for Certification of Transport Category Airplanes, Chapter 6, section 1, paragraph 170.c(8).

9.1.3 AC 27-1, Change 3, Certification of Normal Category Rotorcraft Chapter 3, AC 27 MG 1, paragraph b (10).

9.1.4 AC 29-2, Change 3, Certification of Transport Category Rotorcraft Chapter 3, AC 29 MG 1, paragraph b (10).

9.2 Forward-Looking Windshear Detection.

Follow the TSO instructions to verify performance of the forward-looking windshear function. Installation testing of the forward-looking windshear function often relies on general weather radar functional testing as described in paragraphs 9.1.1 and 9.1.2 of this AC and integration testing versus dedicated forward-looking windshear flight testing.

9.2.1 Penetration Flight Evaluation.

Penetration flights will typically be accomplished by the radar manufacturer as part of the TSO authorization. If penetration data and analysis are available and you determine they are applicable, then you do not need to conduct penetration flight tests. Previously

approved test data generated during the TSO authorization or previous certification effort is acceptable. If forward-looking windshear capability was not previously demonstrated, then verify the detection capability of the forward-looking windshear system by flying in areas of convective activity that can be verified by in-situ measurements, appropriate ground-based radar systems, or the equivalent.

Note: Flying in or near storm cells can be extremely hazardous. Flight crews should exercise good judgment for safe flight based on knowledge of their own abilities and of the capability of the aircraft when considering approaching or penetrating any storm cell or turbulent area.

9.2.2 Clutter Suppression Flight Test.

Evaluate the system’s ability to reject spurious conditions (e.g., clutter suppression, bi/multi-static signal interference, range ambiguous returns, and radome effects). The flight tests may be conducted under visual meteorological conditions. Conduct this evaluation at one or more airports with the following characteristics:

9.2.2.1 Expressways and high-volume surface streets within approximately 1 nm of the runway.

9.2.2.2 Nearby taxiing aircraft.

9.2.2.3 Concentrated urban clutter. The clutter should occupy a minimum area of approximately 1 nm surrounding the airport.

9.3 Turbulence Detection or Atmospheric Threat Awareness.

Follow the TSO installation instructions to verify performance of turbulence detection or atmospheric threat awareness functions. Atmospheric threat awareness functions could include, but are not limited to, hail and lightning indication. Installation testing of these functions often relies on general weather radar functional testing as described in paragraphs 9.1.1 and 9.1.2 of this AC and integration testing versus dedicated flight testing. You should attempt to evaluate the performance of these functions against operationally significant weather when weather is reasonably available and you can do so without placing the aircraft in the hazardous weather. This performance evaluation should ensure the depiction of turbulence or weather hazard is consistent with actual weather phenomenon. Data from the radar manufacturer may be used to supplement or replace additional flight testing if the data is determined to be applicable.

§9.2 references: 9.1.1 and 9.1.2 only.

Also note "parts 23, 25, 27, and 29 aircraft" phrase in §9.1 — evidence the four-category coverage statement belongs to weather radar, not FLS.

content: 某公司拟用同一个多型号改装批准覆盖 Part 23 固定翼和 Part 27 旋翼机，安装同一套带前视风切变功能的气象雷达。理由是“雷达型号和基线数据相同，指导文件也覆盖四类航空器”。请分别判断批准清单的组织方式与前视风切变指导的适用范围。

## 结论

| 判断项 | 结论 |
|---|---|
| 用同一份多型号改装批准（AML-STC）同时覆盖 Part 23 固定翼与 Part 27 旋翼机 | **不可行**。AC 20-180 明确规定 AML-STC 只签发给“同一类别”取证的航空器，并直接举例：按 Part 23 签发的 AML-STC **不能包含**按 Part 25、27 或 29 取证的航空器<kb doc="AC_20-180.pdf" chunk_id="9259d265-e30d-414a-ad08-7f80edd1da54" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" /> |
| “指导文件覆盖四类航空器”使前视风切变指导也覆盖 Part 27 | **不成立**。AC 20-182A 第 1.1 段在“适用于 Part 23、25、27、29 部航空器”之后紧接着限定：对于前视风切变和/或湍流探测能力，**本 AC 的指导仅适用于 Part 25 与 Part 23 固定翼飞机安装**<kb doc="AC_20-182A.pdf" chunk_id="767b9d09-9f10-4d7c-aa91-d1153dbf38c6" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" /> |

即：**设备层面可以共用**（同一 TSO-C63e 型号、同一穿透数据），**批准层面与安装指导层面都不能跨类别共用**。

---

## 一、批准清单的组织方式

### 1. 类别限制是硬性条件，与雷达型号是否相同无关

“An AML-STC is issued for aircraft that are type-certificated in the same category (e.g., an AML-STC for an aircraft certificated under 14 CFR part 23 cannot include aircraft certificated under parts 25, 27, or 29)”<kb doc="AC_20-180.pdf" chunk_id="9259d265-e30d-414a-ad08-7f80edd1da54" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" />。该条不含“除非基线数据相同”之类的例外，因此“雷达型号和基线数据相同”无法绕过它。

### 2. 清单必须逐型号组织，且不能当成一揽子批准

- 必须清楚确立基线数据对**每一个**型号的适用性<kb doc="AC_20-180.pdf" chunk_id="9259d265-e30d-414a-ad08-7f80edd1da54" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" />；
- 每个型号都须表明符合 §21.20 并具备相应数据（型号设计、证实性数据、飞行手册补充），“The AML-STC is not meant to be a blanket approval by allowing additional models without further substantiation.”<kb doc="AC_20-180.pdf" chunk_id="3705aad7-9fcf-4093-9520-acd528861605" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" />；
- 受影响区域的**认证基础与修正案水平须逐型号确定**，FMS 按 §21.5 逐个型号适用<kb doc="AC_20-180.pdf" chunk_id="3705aad7-9fcf-4093-9520-acd528861605" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" />；
- 若型号间安装差异导致相似性与基线数据无法建立，“AML-STC is not the proper method of approval”<kb doc="AC_20-180.pdf" chunk_id="9259d265-e30d-414a-ad08-7f80edd1da54" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" />；固定翼与旋翼机的天线罩、结构、系统集成差异正属于需要重新评估的情形。

### 3. 在 Part 23 内部还应考虑再细分

AC 20-180 建议 Part 23 内的 normal、utility、acrobatic、commuter 各类**分别**签发 AML-STC（因认证要求可能不同），并视改装类型（结构、动力装置、系统、航空电子等）与负责 ACO 协调确定<kb doc="AC_20-180.pdf" chunk_id="9259d265-e30d-414a-ad08-7f80edd1da54" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" />。若连同类内的子类别都要按此谨慎拆分，跨 Part 23/27 合并更无从谈起。

### 4. 清单表格应呈现的结构（据附录 A 模板的列项）

Make、Model/Series、Certification basis/Amendment、TCDS 号、MDL/安装图、FMS、ICA、部件件号、型号特定注记、初始批准日与修订日——每一行对应一个型号及其自身认证基础，见 [[concept/aml-stc|AML-STC]] 与 [[entity/sa01157la|SA01157LA 示例]]。

> 注：本次检索范围内未见针对“多型号批准清单跨类别合并”的其他许可性条款；上述结论限于所采用的 AC 20-180 方法。

---

## 二、前视风切变指导的适用范围

### 1. 文件自身把“四类”与“前视风切变”分开表述

原文：“The guidance is applicable to … parts 23, 25, 27, and 29 aircraft. **For forward-looking windshear and/or turbulence detection capability, the guidance in this AC applies to parts 25 and 23 fixed-wing airplane installations.**”<kb doc="AC_20-182A.pdf" chunk_id="767b9d09-9f10-4d7c-aa91-d1153dbf38c6" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" />

即“四类”是全 AC 的一般适用范围（如 §5.2 显示颜色、§8.3 大气威胁感知告警、§9.1 气象/地面测绘飞行试验），而前视风切变被单独收窄为 **Part 23、Part 25 固定翼**。

### 2. 条款内部相互印证

| 条款 | 引用范围 |
|---|---|
| §9.1 气象与地面测绘雷达飞行试验 | 明确“parts 23, 25, 27, and 29”，并逐部分列出 AC 23-8、AC 25-7、AC 27-1、AC 29-2<kb doc="AC_20-182A.pdf" chunk_id="07ef1485-1cd9-4a11-b027-5460b7cebed0" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" /> |
| §9.2 前视风切变 | 只引用 §9.1.1（AC 23-8）与 §9.1.2（AC 25-7），**未引用** §9.1.3（AC 27-1）与 §9.1.4（AC 29-2）<kb doc="AC_20-182A.pdf" chunk_id="4eab2d62-9985-4443-869e-c73da51c145d" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" /> |
| §6.2.1 前视风切变告警与提示 | 「for **parts 23 and 25** aircraft」，引 §25.1322、AC 25.1322-1、AC 23.1311-1<kb doc="AC_20-182A.pdf" chunk_id="f0cdd104-5906-4bf2-905e-be003c5df91b" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" /> |
| §5.2 显示颜色 | 「parts 23, 25, 27, and 29」，含 AC 27-1、AC 29-2<kb doc="AC_20-182A.pdf" chunk_id="e6347557-1760-4758-90d0-7a32fb315cda" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" /> |

可见“覆盖四类”的表述集中在**通用**条款；一旦进入前视风切变专门章节（§6.2.1、§9.2），适用类别即收窄为 Part 23/25。

### 3. 设备层面统一，不等于安装

# 批准型号清单补充型号合格证

## 文件信息

- 文件类型：Advisory Circular（咨询通告）
- 发布机构：U.S. Department of Transportation, Federal Aviation Administration
- 编号：AC No. 20-180；Change 栏为空
- 日期：08/16/2013
- 发起单位：AIR-110
- 主题：Approved Model List Supplemental Type Certificate (AML-STC)

本咨询通告（AC）提供取得批准型号清单（AML）补充型号合格证（STC）的指南。本AC不是强制性的，也不构成法规。它描述一种可接受的方法，但不是取得AML-STC的唯一方法；如果能够证明另一种方法足以满足要求，可以使用替代方法。但是，如果使用本AC取得批准，则必须遵守其全部条款。

## 适用性

本AC适用于所有已取得型号合格证的飞机和旋翼机。对于发动机和螺旋桨，也可采用同样的批准方法。

本AC自发布之日起对新的AML-STC项目申请生效，不追溯适用于此前已签发的AML-STC。

## 参考文件

- FAA Order 8110.4 — Type Certification
- Title 14 of the Code of Federal Regulations（14 CFR）part 21 — Certification Procedures for Products and Parts
- AC 20-158 — The Certification of Aircraft Electrical and Electronic Systems for Operation in the High-Intensity Radiated Fields (HIRF) Environment
- AC 20-136B — Aircraft Electrical and Electronic System Lightning Protection
- AC 20-155 — SAE Documents to Support Aircraft Lightning Protection Certification
- FAA Order 8110.54B — Instructions for Continued Airworthiness, Responsibilities, Requirements, and Contents
- AC 21-51 — Applicant's Showing of Compliance and Certifying Statement of Compliance

## 背景

标准STC是针对型号设计更改的批准方法，且限于单一型号合格证（TC）。AML-STC是一种多型号批准方法，允许将一套符合性数据（即型号设计数据和证实性数据）指定为“[[concept/baseline-data|基线数据]]”，并适用于各种航空器型号。该方法可适用于同一型号合格证数据表（TCDS）上的多个航空器，或不同TCDS上的多个航空器。

AML-STC适用于安装相同或相似、且各型号之间共享基线数据的情况。它通过避免不必要的试验和重复提交多个型号共用的数据，简化取证工作。如果各型号之间的安装差异导致无法建立相似性和基线数据，则AML-STC不是适当的批准方法。

## AML-STC 要求

AML-STC必须符合14 CFR part 21 subpart E关于签发STC的要求。

- 必须清楚建立基线数据对每一个型号的适用性。
- AML-STC签发给在同一类别中取得型号合格证的航空器（例如，针对按14 CFR part 23取得型号合格证的航空器所签发的AML-STC，不能包含按part 25、part 27或part 29取得型号合格证的航空器）。此外，建议14 CFR part 23内的每一类别（即normal、utility、acrobatic和commuter）分别具有单独的AML-STC，因为这些类别的认证要求可能存在差异。这取决于受影响区域的改装类型（如结构、动力装置、系统、航空电子等）。可能需要与负责的ACO协调，由其审查拟议改装并确定是否有必要为每一类别签发单独的AML-STC，以记录具体的认证要求。
- 必须对AML上的每一个型号表明符合第21.20条的要求及适用数据（如型号设计、证实性数据和飞行手册补充（FMS））。无论该数据来自试验（如飞行试验）还是来自先前批准的重新提交，每个附加航空器型号都需要证实。在增加新型号或修订现有型号时，AML-STC批准允许使用先前已提交的适用符合性数据而无需进一步审查。如果增加与先前批准型号存在差异的新型号，则可能需要进一步证实以处理这些差异。AML-STC不是一种“一揽子”批准，不允许在没有进一步证实的情况下增加型号。
- 针对每个型号确定受改装影响区域的认证基础和修正案水平。
- 对受影响区域的改装不得根据第21.93(b)条对型号合格证产品造成声学变化。
- 飞行手册补充（FMS）需根据第21.5条适用于每个型号。
- AML-STC可能不适用于能够直接控制航空器的系统。例如，自动驾驶仪安装或涉及控制输入的类似系统，无论各型号之间是否共享基线数据，都可能需要在每个拟议型号上进行仔细的设计安装和试验。对于这类安装，可能存在必须逐案评估的、与序列号相关的要求。另一个例子是缩小垂直间隔最小值（RVSM）设备的STC，其中用于RVSM批准的、与型号和序列号相关的静压源误差修正曲线仅适用于单一序列号的航空器。
- 对于寻求AML-STC批准者，尽早与各自的航空器认证办公室（ACO）讨论其计划很重要。为了确定可能影响多型号安装批准的任何未决问题，与ACO的协调是必要的。

## 安装说明与持续适航文件（ICA）

- 安装说明必须充分详细地描述安装，使得后续安装可重复，并在正确遵循时对每个型号形成一致且符合要求的安装。
- 对于更复杂的系统，可能需要更详细的安装说明。任何合适的格式均可使用，包括一个总则部分加上针对个别安装要求的具体型号附录。关键是在取证计划期间作为AML-STC批准的一部分提供这些说明和替代方案。

注：如果某一特定型号存在独特且复杂的安装问题（例如，如何正确地在复合材料结构上穿孔压力容器），则宜寻求新的（非AML）STC批准，使用现有基线数据加上改装产生的任何附加要求。

- 根据14 CFR 21.50，需要符合相应（23、25、27、29、31、33或35）ICA规则的持续适航文件（ICA）。

## 电磁兼容（EMC）、闪电和高强度辐射场（HIRF）考虑

- 随着集成航空电子系统和复合材料结构的使用，对EMC、闪电防护和HIRF防护的评估变得越来越重要。新的HIRF法规于2007年通过，与先前签发的HIRF专用条件存在实质差异。新的闪电法规于2011年通过。在一个航空器型号上不需要考虑HIRF和闪电的安装，在另一个型号上可能需要进一步检查。在铝结构航空器上不需要特定闪电防护的安装，在具有大量复合材料结构的航空器上可能需要进一步检查。为某一航空器执行的标准化试验和类别（如RTCA DO-160中的内容），在没有对另一航空器型号的具体HIRF和闪电鉴定水平作进一步评估的情况下，可能并不适用。对于具有灾难性失效状态的系统，HIRF和闪电符合性可能需要更广泛的符合性证实。
- HIRF和闪电符合性，以及针对某一特定系统在功能危害分析（FHA）和系统安全性评估（SSA）期间所作的假设，可能需要进一步证实。这些事项可能取决于航空器型号，需要FAA与申请人在考虑AML批准之前就符合性方法以及持续适航程序达成一致。

## 使用第三方STC证实AML-STC批准

可能出现这样的情况：原始设备制造商（OEM）将其产品（如地形感知告警系统）出售给航空器制造商或其他最终用户。这些用户通过自己的取证计划，使用OEM的产品取得TC或STC。随后，OEM试图以这些第三方的TC和STC编号作为其表明符合AML-STC要求的唯一方法，来取得AML-STC批准。仅引用第三方TC或STC编号（例如ST016523LA、ST012345SW）而不提供所需的符合性数据（即型号设计数据和证实性数据）是不可接受的。OEM必须作为其自身AML-STC批准的一部分提交符合性数据。

## 型号设计更改

- 对AML-STC的重大更改被视为对型号设计的重大更改，需要FAA批准（如增加型号、修订现有型号）。当STC持有人决定增加新型号或修订现有已批准型号时，FAA或授权的机构指定授权（ODA）将监督AML项目。对AML-STC的轻微更改通常通过证书管理协议（如Partnership for Safety Plan (PSP)）处理，或者由FAA接受申请人或证书持有人处理此类更改的内部流程。
- 存在这样的情况：STC持有人不是向AML增加新型号，而是对AML上的现有硬件或组件进行升级（如软件修订）。在这些情况下，应认真考虑以确保新修订不会产生会影响先前批准的意外后果。例如，软件修订可能在听觉声音或视觉显示方面具有新功能，需要新的飞行机组训练以识别告警和系统故障。这可能影响航空器的运行特性或限制。这些类型的更改可能需要对飞行员工作负荷、人为因素以及修订软件带来的其他后果进行进一步评估。

## 型号拆分

不允许从AML-STC中拆分型号，也不允许将AML-STC拆分为单独STC。AML-STC涉及以最少的数据重复高效、迅速地处理多型号批准。各型号共享基线数据，该基线数据在整个型号清单范围内对每个型号持续适用。一旦通过拆分型号打破这一链条，就需要大量工作来重新建立该特定型号的历史记录（如符合性数据、适航指令、服务通告、问题纸和豁免）。希望将AML-STC转让给第三方（如出售或变更所有权）的设计批准持有人可以整体转让。

## [[concept/configuration-control|构型控制]]

构型控制是跟踪对AML所作全部更改的方法。这些更改可能包括增加新型号或修订现有型号。无论哪种情况，要求都是维护每个型号的相关数据，以便能够验证型号之间的可追溯性和共性。

建议以某种表格形式记录当前构型，以便准确保持AML的构型控制。本AC的附录A提供了可用作模板的AML-STC表格示例。模板中的列是可选的，可以编辑以适应具体项目。这种模板可以提供关于每个安装及其与其他型号关系的宝贵信息。随着更多型号的增加或现有型号的修订，它记录了用于跟踪和保持构型更改的最相关信息。

## 符合性

在取证计划期间，需要按第21.33条进行FAA[[concept/installation-conformity|安装符合性检查]]，以确保部件符合拟议型号设计，并且满足其预期功能。存在这样的情况：增加新型号引入了不属于初始安装符合性范围的更改。这些更改可能需要新的安装符合性，并逐案评估。

## 检查单

为寻求AML-STC批准，需要以下各项：

- 必须对AML上所列的每一个已取证类别的航空器，表明对受影响区域改装的符合性。
- AML上的型号共享相同的基线数据。
- 拟议型号之间存在的安装相似性，以及与其余型号不同的改装区域，均已适当注明。
- 飞行手册补充（FMS）与每个具体型号相关。
- 安装说明足以实现一致且符合要求的安装。
- 已对航空器运行、型别等级和限制的可能影响进行评估。
- 已对多型号批准可能产生的飞行员工作负荷和人为因素影响进行评估。这可能包括由航空器评估组（AEG）的型别评估委员会进行潜在评估，以确定机组工作负荷和训练更改（如正常和应急机组程序）的影响。
- ICA适用于所列的每个型号。

注：根据安装类型和与现有系统的集成程度，必要时可扩充此清单。

## 参考文件获取

可在 http://www.faa.gov/regulations policies/advisory circulars/ 查看所有参考AC的清单，在 http://wvvw.faa.gov/regulations policies/faa regulations/ 查看FAA法规。

1. 2009年2月20日发布的AD涉及因花键过早磨损导致发电机轴剪切（见2011-TAD061-AD）。纠正措施要求按照服务通告56432中所述的 NEW 材料更换轴。服务通告纳入后，件号从-100变为-200，表示改装后状态。

### 说明/定义（Instructions/Definitions）

1. Make as indicated on TCDS：在此列输入制造商名称（Boeing、Douglas等）。
2. Model as indicated on TCDS：在此列输入航空器型号及适用的后续系列。某些安装是型号/系列特定的，应在AML中记录。
3. Certification basis：在此列输入受改装影响区域的认证基础和修正案水平。
4. TCDS：在此列输入TCDS编号和最后修订水平。
5. Master Drawing List (MDL)/Installation Drawing：在此列输入申请人的安装图纸或MDL及修订号（以适用者为准）。通常，申请人使用这两种文件之一进行构型控制；如果能够达到可追溯性和构型控制的目的，也允许使用其他文件替代。
6. Flight Manual Supplement (FMS)：在此列列入对现有飞行手册的补充章节修订水平和批准日期。每个具体型号可能有多个补充章节添加到AFM。
7. ICA：在此列输入文件编号及修订水平和日期。
8. Component Manufacturer (P/N)：在此列输入制造商名称和部件件号，或为确保所有型号安装包含相同部件而认为必要的任何其他信息。
9. Model Specific Note：在此列输入针对该部件（仅部件，而非整架航空器）发布的任何信息，如适航指令（AD）和服务通告（SB）。输入对审查者批准AML有帮助或重要的任何附加信息、限制或条件。
10. Initial Approved Date：在此列输入每个型号的初始批准日期。如果申请人按后续顺序增加型号，该日期对每个型号可能不同。
11. Amended date：在此列输入具体型号的修订批准日期（如适用）。

注：从最新批准的型号（即初始批准日期）开始置于表格顶部，并按批准日期（2012、2011、2010、2009、2008等）顺序列出先前型号。

## Key Takeaways

- AC 20-180（2013年8月16日）是FAA咨询通告，不是强制性要求，也不构成法规；它描述一种可接受的AML-STC取得方法，若使用则须遵守其全部条款。
- AML-STC允许用一套基线数据覆盖同一或不同TCDS上的多个航空器型号，以减少重复试验和数据重复提交；若安装差异导致无法建立相似性和基线数据，则不适用。
- AML-STC只能覆盖同一类别的航空器；part 23内不同类别是否分别签发，取决于改装类型并可能需要与ACO协调确定。
- 每个型号均须表明符合第21.20条并具备相应数据（型号设计、证实性数据、FMS）；增加具有差异的新型号可能需要进一步证实。
- 直接控制航空器的系统（如自动驾驶仪、RVSM设备）可能不适合AML-STC，可能需要逐案或逐序列号评估。
- 禁止拆分型号或将AML-STC拆分为单独STC；允许整体转让。
- 构型控制建议以表格形式记录，附录A给出可作模板的AML-STC示例表及相应说明/定义。

# 机载气象雷达系统测试与评估

本页依据 AC 20-182A（文件号原文标注为 AC 20-182A1，日期 10/1/16）第 9 节“TEST AND EVALUATION”，规定气象雷达装机后的测试评估流程，覆盖天线罩、显示与告警优先级、故障检测、人因接口及系统间干扰等验证项目。

## 9 测试与评估

本节为飞机上的雷达系统测试提供指导。若雷达系统为气象与地面测绘雷达，按 9.1 执行；若雷达系统包含前视风切变探测功能，按 9.2 执行；若雷达系统包含湍流探测或[[concept/atmospheric-threat-awareness-functions|大气威胁感知功能]]，按 9.3 执行。

所有雷达系统的测试应确保：

- 雷达天线与天线罩组合功能正常；
- 雷达显示与告警优先级功能正常，且告警、告警抑制、提示（annunciations）与控制功能正常；
- 故障检测功能正常工作；
- 人机因素接口可接受；
- 雷达不会对其他系统产生不利干扰；
- 其他系统不会对雷达产生不利干扰。

## 9.1 气象雷达

气象与地面测绘脉冲雷达功能的飞行测试，应按下列 AC 的最新修订版执行，适用于第 23、25、27、29 部航空器：

- 9.1.1 AC 23-8《Flight Test Guide for Certification of Part 23 Airplanes》，Chapter 5，paragraph 1.b (10)。
- 9.1.2 AC 25-7《Flight Test Guide for Certification of Transport Category Airplanes》，Chapter 6，section 1，paragraph 170.c(8)。
- 9.1.3 AC 27-1, Change 3《Certification of Normal Category Rotorcraft》，Chapter 3，AC 27 MG 1，paragraph b (10)。
- 9.1.4 AC 29-2, Change 3《Certification of Transport Category Rotorcraft》，Chapter 3，AC 29 MG 1，paragraph b (10)。

## 9.2 前视风切变探测

按 TSO 说明验证前视风切变功能的性能。前视风切变功能的装机测试通常依赖本 AC 第 9.1.1 和 9.1.2 段所述的一般气象雷达功能测试以及集成测试，而非专门的前视风切变飞行测试。

### 9.2.1 穿透飞行评估（Penetration Flight Evaluation）

穿透飞行通常由雷达制造商作为 TSO 授权的一部分完成。如果穿透数据和分析可用，且判定其适用，则无需进行穿透飞行测试；在 TSO 授权或以往取证工作中生成的先前已批准测试数据可被接受。如果此前未演示过前视风切变能力，则应通过在对流活动区域飞行来验证前视风切变系统的探测能力，该区域可通过原位测量、适当的陆基雷达系统或等效手段加以核实。

注：在风暴单体内部或附近飞行可能极其危险。在考虑接近或穿透任何风暴单体或湍流区域时，飞行机组应基于对自身能力和飞机能力的了解，运用良好判断以确保飞行安全。

### 9.2.2 杂波抑制飞行测试

评估系统抑制虚假条件的能力（例如杂波抑制、双/多基地信号干扰、距离模糊回波以及天线罩效应）。飞行测试可在目视气象条件下进行。应在一个或多个具有下列特征的机场开展该项评估：

- 9.2.2.1 跑道约 1 nm 范围内的高速公路与高流量地面道路。
- 9.2.2.2 附近的滑行飞机。
- 9.2.2.3 集中的城市杂波。杂波应占据机场周围最小约 1 nm 的面积。

## 9.3 湍流探测或大气威胁感知

按 TSO 装机说明验证湍流探测或大气威胁感知功能的性能。大气威胁感知功能可包括但不限于冰雹和闪电指示。这些功能的装机测试通常依赖本 AC 第 9.1.1 和 9.1.2 段所述的一般气象雷达功能测试以及集成测试，而非专门的飞行测试。在天气条件合理可得且不会使飞机进入危险天气的前提下，应尝试针对运行上有意义的天气评估这些功能的性能。该性能评估应确保湍流或天气威胁的显示与实际天气现象一致。如果判定雷达制造商的数据适用，可用其补充或替代额外的飞行测试。

## 解析说明

- 原文摘录标注为“AC No: 20-182A1”，与可用条目“AC 20-182A”存在编号差异，本页保留原文编号表述。
- 9.2 与 9.3 中“依赖一般气象雷达功能测试（9.1.1、9.1.2）加集成测试”为原文对装机测试方式的描述；9.2.1 关于穿透数据的豁免以“数据可用且判定适用”为条件。
- 原文未给出 9.2.2 各机场特征以外的具体判据或通过/失败标准。

<content>
# 前视风切变探测与告警显示

本页内容来自 AC 20-182A1（2016年10月1日）。该 AC 就符合最新修订版 TSO-C63《Airborne Weather Radar Equipment》的机载气象雷达系统的初始批准和后续批准提供指导；就前视风切变探测能力而言，该 AC 的指导适用于 14 CFR 第 25 部和第 23 部固定翼飞机安装。该 AC 不是强制要求，也不构成法规；它描述的是可接受的符合性方法之一，但不是唯一方法；若采用该 AC 所述方法，则必须在所有重要方面遵循该 AC。附录 A 提供前视风切变系统告警、提示和显示图标的补充指导。

## 背景：与 TSO-C63e 及 SLR 10.2 的关系

前视风切变探测功能已纳入 TSO-C63e。该 AC 纳入并澄清了相应的适航指导，并消除 System Level Requirements (SLR) 10.2“Airborne Short and Long Range Windshear Predictive Systems (Forward-Looking Windshear Systems) Interim Certification Requirements, Revision 10.2”中的勘误。对于符合 TSO-C63e 或其后版本的系统，SLR 10.2 不再适用。

## 前视风切变激活

- 为允许因风切变条件及时中止起飞，应确保前视风切变功能能够在起飞滑跑开始前人工激活。
- 应确保前视风切变功能为起飞自动激活，以提供及时的起飞警告。
- 当前视风切变功能启用时，应确保系统在下降进近过程中自动激活，无需飞行机组干预，其激活高度足以按本 AC 第 6.2.2 段提供视觉和听觉告警。
- 在复飞或连续起降（touch and go）情况下，前视风切变探测系统可重置到相应模式（着陆或起飞）。
- 某些系统构型利用应答机模式自动激活雷达，以便在飞行机组未人工激活雷达时仍能在起飞期间提供前视风切变告警。该构型形成于应答机在飞机滑上跑道前才开启、离开跑道后才关闭的年代；但随着 Airport Surface Detection Equipment-Model X (ASDE-X) 雷达和 Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast (ADS-B) 的出现，飞行机组现在滑行时通常保持应答机“开启”。这可能对地面处理飞机的人员构成危险，因为飞机引导员和牵引车操作员常在极接近机头雷达罩的位置作业。应考虑此类运行或风切变功能任何自动地面激活特性，对前视风切变功能的自动激活特性进行危险评估。

## 前视风切变告警要求

- 必须确保告警和提示遵循飞机的驾驶舱告警理念，并遵守法规及下列 AC 最新修订版中针对第 23 部和第 25 部飞机的指导：14 CFR § 25.1322, Flight Crew Alerting；AC 25.1322-1, Flight Crew Alerting；AC 23.1311-1, Installation of Electronic Display in Part 23 Airplanes。
- 必须确保集成系统能够发出附录 A 表 1 中所述的全部前视风切变 Advisory、Caution 和 Warning 提示与告警。
- 必须确保在下列任一条件存在时发出视觉文本警告：听觉告警正在发出；威胁超过告警阈值；或威胁存在于 TSO-C63 最新修订版所定义的区域内。
- 应确保风切变探测能力失效的提示在飞行机组正常坐姿位置即可见。

## 前视风切变告警抑制

- 起飞期间，系统应在旋转（rotation）之前某一规定的飞机速度抑制所有新的听觉和视觉告警，并在离地后重新启用告警能力。应按安装手册说明设置起飞告警设置，并确保抑制与机型特定的起飞告警抑制准则一致。
- 最后进近期间，应确保所有新的系统听觉和视觉 caution 与 warning 告警在离地高度（AGL）50 英尺至接地之间被抑制。
- 应确保所有新的听觉和视觉 warning 与 caution 告警在 1200 英尺 AGL 以上被抑制。

## 前视风切变告警优先级

- 应遵循本 AC 第 5.5 段关于飞机告警优先级的指导。
- 若在同时装有[[entity/reactive-windshear-system|反应式风切变系统]]的飞机上安装前视风切变系统，应确保反应式风切变系统的 caution 告警被禁用。若前视风切变系统不工作，发出反应式风切变 caution 告警是可接受的。
- 注：反应式风切变系统的 warning 告警应保持启用。

## 显示要求

- 允许在系统处于风切变模式预位的任何高度显示风切变图标。
- 风切变图标由红黑相间的条组成。各条应定向为以顶点为中心的圆弧。使用红色是合适的，以便与下方的黄色气象显示形成视觉区分。附录 A 图 1 给出若干前视风切变图标示例。
- 应确保每个条的深度使风切变图标相对于其他显示信息足够醒目。
- 若飞行机组所选显示距离大于 5 海里（nm），且该距离选择使飞行机组无法将风切变符号与其他显示信息区分，则应确保琥珀色/黄色径向线从图标延伸至显示上边缘，以帮助区分风切变符号。为适应方位范围较宽的图标（或图标组），允许限制径向线之间的宽度；因此，径向线可沿位于图标左、右径向边界内侧的方位线延伸。
- 若使用其他风切变符号，则应证明该符号为飞行机组提供清晰且实质的收益。
- 当探测到风切变威胁时，相应显示可自动呈现或由飞行机组操作选择。若仅提供人工选择，则应确保按正常操作程序配置驾驶舱时，人工呈现风切变显示所需的飞行机组工作量最小，且不超过一个操作动作。

## 表 1：前视风切变系统提示、告警与显示

| Alert Level | Advisory | Caution | Warning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Visual Textual Alert | None | Amber/Yellow Visual Textual Annunciation (or lamp): “Windshear” or “Windshear Ahead” or “W/S Ahead” | Red Visual Textual Annunciation (or lamp): “Windshear” or “Windshear Ahead” or “W/S Ahead” |
| Aural Alert | None | Distinctive Aural Alert: Chime or message; not containing the word windshear. Example: Tone “Whoop” or “Monitor Radar Display” | Voice Alert: Takeoff: “Windshear Ahead, Windshear Ahead” Approach or Go-around: “Go Around, Windshear Ahead” |
| Icon | Icon symbology as defined in Section 6.5. | Icon symbology as defined in Section 6.5. | Icon symbology as defined in Section 6.5. |

注 1：前视风切变图标作为气象危险位置指示提供，而不是告警。其颜色与 AC 25.1322-1 第 11 节或 AC 25-11 最新修订版不冲突。

注 2：前视风切变 caution 告警可能依风切变危险的位置发展为时间紧迫（time-critical）的 windshear warning 告警。

![Figure 1. Forward-Looking Windshear System Icon Examples
Note: These images are provided only as examples of possible icon implementations. Other implementations may be used. Refer to the manufacturer installation and operations manual for icon implementation.](http://localhost:8080/api/v1/ingestion/jobs/fe60cb971dff466c96698251222ba819/assets/6f6c47f181b712292626)

![Figure 2. Examples of Windshear Icon Radial Lines](http://localhost:8080/api/v1/ingestion/jobs/fe60cb971dff466c96698251222ba819/assets/68eff46f9ce8f6cb6130)

图 1 注：这些图像仅作为可能图标实现的示例提供，也可采用其他实现方式；图标实现请参阅制造商安装与操作手册。

## 测试与评估：前视风切变探测

若雷达系统包含前视风切变探测功能，应按本 AC 第 9.2 节执行。前视风切变功能的性能验证应遵循 TSO 说明。前视风切变功能的安装测试通常依赖第 9.1.1 段（AC 23-8, Chapter 5, paragraph 1.b(10)）和第 9.1.2 段（AC 25-7, Chapter 6, section 1, paragraph 170.c(8)）所述的一般气象雷达功能测试，以及集成测试，而非专门的前视风切变飞行测试。

### 穿越飞行评估（Penetration Flight Evaluation）

穿越飞行通常由雷达制造商作为 TSO 授权的一部分完成。若穿越数据和分析可用，且确定其适用，则无需进行穿越飞行测试。在 TSO 授权或以往取证工作中生成的先前已批准测试数据是可接受的。若前视风切变能力此前未经演示，则应通过在可被原位测量、适当的地面雷达系统或等效手段验证的对流活动区域飞行，来验证前视风切变系统的探测能力。

注：在风暴单体内部或附近飞行可能极其危险。飞行机组在考虑接近或穿越任何风暴单体或湍流区域时，应基于对自身能力及飞机能力的了解，作出安全飞行的良好判断。

### 杂波抑制飞行测试

评估系统抑制虚假条件的能力（例如杂波抑制、双/多基地信号干扰、距离模糊回波以及雷达罩效应）。飞行测试可在目视气象条件下进行。应在一个或多个具有下列特征的机场进行该评估：

- 跑道约 1 nm 范围内有高速公路和高流量地面道路；
- 附近有滑行中的飞机；
- 集中的城市杂波，该杂波应在机场周围占据最小约 1 nm 的面积。

## 解析说明

- 原文摘录标注的编号为“AC No: 20-182A1”，日期为 10/1/16。
- 表 1 中“Icon”行三个告警级别均引用 Section 6.5，图标细节见第 6.5 节及附录 A 图 1、图 2；图像仅为例示，实际实现以制造商安装与操作手册为准。
- 摘录未提供本 AC 中附录 A 图 1、图 2 所对应图标的具体图形数值，本页不作推测。
- 本页仅涵盖前视风切变相关条款；同一 AC 中气象与地面测绘雷达、湍流探测、大气威胁感知及 AFM/S 等内容属其他主题，不在本页范围内。

<summary>
本页说明AML-STC中的“基线数据”概念，即跨多个航空器型号共享的型号设计数据与符合性验证数据，并整理其适用性、共享与拆分限制等原文要求。

<content>
# 基线数据

**基线数据**：在AML-STC中，指可适用于多个飞机型号的型号设计数据和符合性数据，是跨型号共享并减少重复审定的核心。

## 背景中的定义

标准STC是一种针对型号设计更改的批准方法，但其适用范围限于单一型号合格证（TC）。AML-STC则是一种多型号批准方法：它允许将一套符合性数据（即型号设计数据和符合性验证数据）指定为“baseline data”（基线数据），并将该基线数据适用于多个航空器型号。该方法可适用于同一型号合格证数据表（TCDS）上的多个航空器，也可适用于不同TCDS上的多个航空器。

AML-STC适用于安装方案相同或相似、且各型号之间共享基线数据的情况。其目的是减少重复试验和重复提交多个型号共用的数据，从而简化取证工作。如果各型号之间的安装差异导致无法建立相似性或基线数据，则AML-STC不是适当的批准方法。

## 各型号适用性的建立

AML-STC必须符合14 CFR part 21 subpart E关于签发STC的要求。其中，必须清楚建立基线数据对每一个型号的适用性（The applicability of the baseline data for each model must clearly be established）。

## 符合性数据的共享与补充证实

对AML清单上的每一个型号，都必须表明符合第21.20条的要求并提供适用数据（例如型号设计、符合性验证数据和飞行手册补充（FMS））。无论这些数据来自试验（如飞行试验），还是来自此前批准的重新提交，每个新增航空器型号均需提供证实。

在增加新型号或修订现有型号时，AML-STC批准允许使用此前已提交且适用的符合性数据，而无需进一步审查。如果新增型号与先前批准的型号存在差异，则可能需要进一步证实以处理这些差异。AML-STC并非“一揽子批准”，不允许在没有进一步证实的情况下增加型号。

## 基线数据的局限情形

AML-STC可能不适用于可直接控制航空器的系统。例如，自动驾驶仪安装或涉及控制输入的类似系统，无论各型号之间是否共享基线数据，都可能在每个拟议型号上需要仔细的设计安装和测试；此类安装可能存在需逐案评估的、与序列号相关的特定要求。另一例子是缩小垂直间隔最小值（RVSM）设备的STC：用于RVSM批准的、与型号和序列号相关的静压源误差修正曲线仅适用于单一序列号航空器。

对于存在独特且复杂安装问题的特定型号，宜利用现有基线数据加上改装产生的任何附加要求，寻求新的（非AML）STC批准。

## [[concept/configuration-control|构型控制]]中的基线数据

构型控制一节要求：AML清单上的型号共享同一基线数据（Model(s) on the AML share the same baseline data）；并须正确注明拟议型号之间存在的安装相似性，以及改装中与其他型号不同的那些区域。

## [[concept/model-splitting-restriction|型号拆分限制]]

不允许从AML-STC中拆分型号，也不允许将AML-STC拆分为单独STC。AML-STC的意义在于以最少的数据重复，高效、迅速地处理多型号批准；各型号共享基线数据，且该基线数据在整个型号清单范围内对每个型号持续适用。一旦拆分型号而破坏这一链条，就需要大量工作重新建立该特定型号的历史记录（例如符合性数据、适航指令、服务通告、问题纸和豁免）。设计批准持有人可以将AML-STC整体转让给第三方（例如出售或变更所有权）。

## 说明

以上内容来自[[entity/faa-ac-20-180|FAA咨询通告AC 20-180]]（2013年8月16日）。该咨询通告不是强制性要求，也不构成法规；它描述一种可接受的方法，但不是取得AML-STC的唯一方法。若申请人选择使用本AC取得批准，则必须遵守其全部条款。

# AC 20-182A 咨询通告

美国联邦航空管理局（FAA）咨询通告。主题：Airworthiness Approval for Aircraft Weather Radar Systems（[[concept/aircraft-weather-radar-airworthiness-approval|机载气象雷达系统适航批准]]）。日期：10/1/16。发起部门：AIR–130。编号：AC No: 20-182A。

## 1 目的（WHAT IS THE PURPOSE OF THIS ADVISORY CIRCULAR (AC)?）

1.1 本咨询通告（AC）为符合最新修订版 TSO-C63《Airborne Weather Radar Equipment》的机载气象雷达系统的初始批准和后续适航批准提供指导。本 AC 涵盖具有气象探测与地面测绘、前视风切变探测、[[concept/forward-looking-turbulence-detection|前视湍流探测]]以及大气威胁感知能力的飞机雷达系统。本指导适用于 Title 14 of the Code of Federal Regulations（14 CFR）第 23、25、27、29 部航空器。对于前视风切变和/或湍流探测能力，本 AC 的指导适用于第 25 部和第 23 部固定翼飞机安装。

1.2 本 AC 不是强制要求，也不构成法规。本 AC 描述了完成机载气象雷达设备安装适航批准的一种可接受方法，但不是唯一方法。但是，如果使用本 AC 所述方法，则必须在所有重要方面遵循它。附录 A 提供关于前视风切变系统告警、提示和显示图标的补充指导。相关文件清单见本 AC 附录 B。

1.3 本 AC 提供的指导针对新批准。本 AC 不打算修改、改变或取消现有设备设计或适航批准。具有现有批准的设备可以在其原始设计和适航认证的规定范围内继续安装。

## 2 适用对象（WHO DOES THIS AC AFFECT?）

本 AC 适用于寻求飞机气象雷达系统适航批准的申请人。该适航批准可以在型号合格证（TC）、补充型号合格证（STC）、修订型号合格证（ATC）或修订补充型号合格证（ASTC）下获得批准。

## 3 是否取消先前 AC（DOES THIS AC CANCEL ANY PRIOR AC?）

本 AC 取消 2014 年 6 月 17 日发布的 AC 20-182。

## 4 背景（BACKGROUND）

### 4.1 具有前视风切变探测功能的机载多普勒气象雷达系统

前视风切变探测功能已纳入 TSO-C63e。本 AC 纳入并澄清适当的适航指导，并消除 System Level Requirements（SLR）10.2 “Airborne Short and Long Range Windshear Predictive Systems (Forward-Looking Windshear Systems) Interim Certification Requirements, Revision 10.2” 中的勘误。SLR 10.2 不再适用于符合 TSO-C63e 或更新版本的系统。

### 4.2 具有前视湍流探测功能的机载多普勒气象雷达系统

2012 年 2 月之前，FAA 使用由 Airborne Turbulence Detection Systems（ATDS）Working Group 制定的设计标准，以及记录在 issue papers 中的适航要求，来认证前视湍流探测雷达。FAA 于 2012 年 2 月发布 TSO-C63d，纳入了 ATDS Working Group 的设计要求。随着 TSO-C63e 的发布，湍流探测功能继续包含在 TSO 中。本 AC 将 issue papers 中剩余的适航指导纳入正式发布的 FAA 指导。

## 一、批准清单的组织方式

### 1. 类别限制是硬性条件，与雷达型号是否相同无关

“An AML-STC is issued for aircraft that are type-certificated in the same category (e.g., an AML-STC for an aircraft certificated under 14 CFR part 23 cannot include aircraft certificated under parts 25, 27, or 29)”<kb doc="AC_20-180.pdf" chunk_id="9259d265-e30d-414a-ad08-7f80edd1da54" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" />。该条不含“除非基线数据相同”之类的例外，因此“雷达型号和基线数据相同”无法绕过它。

### 2. 清单必须逐型号组织，且不能当成一揽子批准

- 必须清楚确立基线数据对**每一个**型号的适用性<kb doc="AC_20-180.pdf" chunk_id="9259d265-e30d-414a-ad08-7f80edd1da54" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" />；
- 每个型号都须表明符合 §21.20 并具备相应数据（型号设计、证实性数据、飞行手册补充），“The AML-STC is not meant to be a blanket approval by allowing additional models without further substantiation.”<kb doc="AC_20-180.pdf" chunk_id="3705aad7-9fcf-4093-9520-acd528861605" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" />；
- 受影响区域的**认证基础与修正案水平须逐型号确定**，FMS 按 §21.5 逐个型号适用<kb doc="AC_20-180.pdf" chunk_id="3705aad7-9fcf-4093-9520-acd528861605" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" />；
- 若型号间安装差异导致相似性与基线数据无法建立，“AML-STC is not the proper method of approval”<kb doc="AC_20-180.pdf" chunk_id="9259d265-e30d-414a-ad08-7f80edd1da54" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" />；固定翼与旋翼机的天线罩、结构、系统集成差异正属于需要重新评估的情形。

### 3. 在 Part 23 内部还应考虑再细分

AC 20-180 建议 Part 23 内的 normal、utility、acrobatic、commuter 各类**分别**签发 AML-STC（因认证要求可能不同），并视改装类型（结构、动力装置、系统、航空电子等）与负责 ACO 协调确定<kb doc="AC_20-180.pdf" chunk_id="9259d265-e30d-414a-ad08-7f80edd1da54" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" />。若连同类内的子类别都要按此谨慎拆分，跨 Part 23/27 合并更无从谈起。

### 4. 清单表格应呈现的结构（据附录 A 模板的列项）

Make、Model/Series、Certification basis/Amendment、TCDS 号、MDL/安装图、FMS、ICA、部件件号、型号特定注记、初始批准日与修订日——每一行对应一个型号及其自身认证基础，见 [[concept/aml-stc|AML-STC]] 与 [[entity/sa01157la|SA01157LA 示例]]。
