<context id="1">5. OPERATIONAL CONSIDERATIONS.

5.1 Polar Operations. The polar region environment is defined as the area beginning at 5^° to 30º latitude from the pole, depending on location, and extending to either the north or south pole. Anomalies with the earth’s magnetic field in the polar region can provide erroneous magnetic heading indications. Aircraft will typically use true heading information when flying in Polar Regions.

5.1.1 If the AHRS article is installed on aircraft intended to operate in the Polar Regions, the applicant should conduct a flight test demonstration to show proper operation for new AHRS articles or show previous successful flight test demonstration in an aircraft of like or similar installation. If the AHRS article was flight tested under the combined TSO-STC process, then the applicant should ensure the aircraft complies with the TSO article installation limitations and STC. Simulation testing and/or analysis are acceptable methods of compliance for follow-on installations.

5.1.2 Ensure a means is provided to identify when true heading is selected, such as information on the display or marking on a control panel.

5.1.3 Evaluate any automatic switching from magnetic to true heading or vice versa while entering and exiting Polar Regions. If the automatic switching between magnetic/true heading is not sufficiently self-evident, a suitable alerting or other annunciation should accompany the automatic switching.

5.1.4 Ensure the flight manual is updated with any unique procedures for landing, departing and flying the aircraft in Polar Regions.

5.1.5 If AHRS performance degrades in the polar region a visual indication should be provided to the flightcrew. An aural annunciation may be provided as well, depending on the specific system design and overall flight deck philosophy. Any annunciation should be clear, unambiguous, timely and attention getting; should only be indicated while the condition exists; should be consistently located in a specific area of the electronic display; and be located in the flight crew’s primary field of view when immediate flightcrew awareness is required.

5.1.6 If the AHRS is not qualified to fly in the polar region, ensure the A/RFMS includes the appropriate limitations.

5.2 Areas of High Magnetic Disturbances. High magnetic disturbance areas can be caused by aircraft carriers, power lines, elevated helicopter-landing platforms, buried concrete steel reinforcing bars, ground equipment in close proximity to the aircraft, or a myriad of other conditions.

5.2.1 When an AHRS installation includes a flux valve or magnetometer, evaluate the functionalities below used to compensate for magnetic disturbance if they are included with the AHRS installation.

a) A DG mode which temporarily deactivates the flux valve or magnetometer;

b) A manual alignment mode allowing the pilot to manually align the affected system in an area away from the magnetic interference;

c) Rapid alignment capability once the magnetic interference is gone; or,

d) Automatic reversion. Automatic reversion may be required for those installations where Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) systems and oil drilling platforms are normal landing areas to meet the applicable safety requirements. A timed, free gyro mode (DG or similar) may be acceptable. Ensure the system is available at landing and initial alignment or allows an alternate short-term un-slaved mode with a set-heading alignment capability. A ground or flight test will need to be conducted to evaluate the operational and performance capability.

5.2.2 Evaluate the installation of the flux valve or magnetometer in a representative environment to ensure magnetic disturbances are minimized.

5.2.3 Evaluate the effects of power-up, initial alignment, take offs, and landings from areas of high magnetic disturbance, when applicable.

5.2.4 Ensure instructions for the rapid alignment, manual and automatic reversion modes are added to the flight manual or pilot’s operating handbook (POH).

5.2.5 Ensure instructions are added to the flight manual or POH identifying the potential for magnetic disturbances, when applicable.

5.3 Low Power Setting. Evaluate low power engine settings and possible associated low voltage conditions to determine if they affect AHRS performance. This evaluation is necessary because the FAA has identified concerns with low power settings causing fluctuations and erroneous orientations of heading and attitude displays. Ensure any resulting limitations are addressed in the A/RFMS or POH.

5.4 Wind Speeds. Some AHRS use wind calculations to correct the heading information. Depending on the magnetic variation and algorithms, some are more sensitive to changes in wind speed and direction than others. For aircraft using these corrections and flying in or around tropical areas or polar jet streams between 18,000 ft - 40,000 ft Mean Sea Level (MSL), ensure AHRS operability for these regimes. Also, evaluate these systems at lower aircraft speeds near stall with high headwind components. If testing with the unique wind dynamics is not possible, then the installer should provide some means of analysis to ensure the system is capable of operating with no adverse safety issues and provide any limitations in the A/RFMS. If the AHRS integrates with a windshear system, verify operational capability and limitations.

5.5 Rotorcraft Considerations. Some AHRS have a difficult time distinguishing between rotorcraft movement and the normal vibration spectrum of the platform to which it is mounted. Manufacturers of this technology have different approaches on how to “filter” these inputs so an accurate attitude solution can be derived. Other solutions are possible, but listed are a few accepted approaches.

a) One approach relies on surveying the vibration spectrum of the applicable installation area by conducting a series of flight test evaluations. Based on data obtained during these flight tests, adjustments are made to the software logic to allow the system to adequately distinguish valid from invalid inputs (i.e., those resulting from the rotorcraft’s normal vibration). This approach results in the need to create a specific part number for each installation.

b)	 Another approach relies on the use of GNSS and vector data to “stabilize and correct” the attitude solution.

d)	 A third approach relies on the use of pitot static information to help correct and stabilize the accelerometer derived attitude solution. AHRS designed with MEMS technology using TSO-C16 pitot/static corrections, may not be sufficient for rotorcraft AHRS applications. Operational rotorcraft maneuvers differ in performance from fixed wing aircraft, because they involve roll, pitch, and yaw rates coupled with translations in all directions to a stationary hover. For rotorcraft applications, ensure the pitot system, if used, provides the needed inputs with the appropriate accuracy, integrity, and availability. If necessary, demonstrate or evaluate the performance of the pitot system especially in low speeds, where pitot/static data may affect the reliability and integrity of the attitude solution. If it does affect the attitude solution, a limitation on the operation may apply.

<context id="2">U.S. Department of Transportation Federal Aviation Administration

Advisory Circular

Subject: AIRWORTHINESS APPROVAL OF ATTITUDE HEADING REFERENCE SYSTEM (AHRS) EQUIPMENT

Date: 4/7/14

AC No: 20-181

Initiated By: AIR-130

1. GENERAL INFORMATION.

1.1 Purpose. This advisory circular (AC) supplements existing airworthiness approval guidance for attitude heading reference system (AHRS) articles approved under technical standard order (TSO)-C201, Attitude Heading Reference System, or later revisions. TSO-C201 includes performance standards for non-gimbaled attitude, heading, and turn and slip systems. Appendix A contains a list of acronyms. Appendix B explains where to obtain reference documents. Refer to the latest revision of following list of ACs to complete the aircraft type specific primary or stand-by flight instrument airworthiness certification process:

a)	 AC 20-167, Airworthiness Approval of Enhanced Vision Systems, Synthetic Vision Systems, Combined Vision Systems, and Enhanced Flight Vision Systems;

b) AC 23-8, Flight Test Guide for Certification of Part 23 Airplanes;

c) AC 23-17, Systems and Equipment Guide for Certification of Part 23 Airplane and Airships;

d) AC 23.1309-1, System Safety Analysis and Assessment for Part 23 Airplanes;

e) AC 23.1311-1, Installation of Electronic Displays in Part 23 Airplanes;

f) AC 25-7, Flight Test Guidance for Part 25 Airplanes;

g) AC 25-11, Electronic Flight Deck Displays;

h) AC 25.1302-1, Installed Systems and Equipment for Use by the Flightcrew;

i) AC 25.1309-1, System Design and Analysis;

j) AC 25.1322-1, Flightcrew Alerting;

k) AC 25.1329-1, Approval of Flight Guidance Systems;

l) AC 27-1, Certification of Normal Category Rotorcraft; and

m) AC 29-2, Certification of Transport Category Rotorcraft.

1.2 Related CFR Regulations. Title 14 of the Code of Federal Regulations (14 CFR)

a)	 Part 23, §§ 23.1301, .1303, .1309, .1311, .1321, .1322, and .1327.

b)	 Part 25, §§ 25.1301, .1302, .1303, .1309, .1321, .1322, .1327, .1333, .1523 and Appendix D.

c)	 Part 27, §§ 27.1301, .1303, .1309, .1321, .1322, .1327, and Appendix B.

d)	 Part 29, §§ 29.1301, .1303, .1309, .1321, .1322, .1327, .1333, and Appendix B

1.3 Audience. This AC provides guidance for aircraft manufacturers, avionics manufacturers, installation shops, or other applicants seeking airworthiness approval under type certificate (TC), amended type certificate (ATC), supplemental type certificate (STC), or amended supplemental type certificate (ASTC) for TSO-C201 AHRS equipment.

1.4 Background. Manufacturers of attitude (pitch and roll), heading, turn and slip instruments have used TSO-C3, TSO-C4, TSO-C5, and TSO-C6 standards, dating back to 1958. More recently, AHRS based on micro-electro-mechanical systems (MEMS), ring-laser gyros (RLG), fiber optic gyros (FOG), and other technologies, are replacing conventional attitude and heading instruments to increase data performance reliability and accuracy. AHRS provides attitude and heading measurements with both static and dynamic accuracy comparable to traditional gimbaled systems. TSO-C201 does not cancel the older TSOs, but has been written for the non-gimbaled attitude and heading systems. When we published TSO-C201, many airworthiness approval policies existed for primary and stand-by flight instrumentation for each aircraft category type, as listed in Section 1.1. Although comprehensive, those policies do not address certain features included in TSO-C201 which require evaluation at installation. This AC's supplemental guidance addresses four specific areas:

a)	 Aiding Sources;

b)	 Degraded Mode;

c)	 TSO-C201 Categorizations and Applications; and,

d)	 Operational Considerations.

2. AHRS AIDING SOURCES. An AHRS aiding source is an internal or external system which provides additional sensor information to the core strap down attitude heading reference function. Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) and air data computer (ADC) aiding sources are commonly used to identify aircraft accelerations to reduce errors in the attitude function. Flux valves and magnetometers provide magnetic reference for heading functions, and numerous sources can be used for performance monitoring. Some aiding designs only supplement the AHRS functionality, and loss of aiding may only have limited effect on AHRS performance. On other designs, aiding may provide integral information where loss of the aiding source could lead to loss of AHRS functionality.

2.1 Internal Aiding Source Installations. Evaluate internal aiding sources as part of the overall article’s intended function evaluation. The internal aiding source should be qualified as part of the TSO-C201 design approval process. Ensure the aiding source provides the needed inputs with the appropriate accuracy, integrity, availability, and software level and electronic hardware design

assurance for its intended use. For example, if the system was developed for a general aviation aircraft, but will be installed on a commuter aircraft, then the internal aiding source may need to be re-evaluated to ensure the appropriate compatibility with the aircraft’s design architecture and its usage.

2.2 External Aiding Source Installations. This paragraph applies to external aiding sources not qualified as part of the TSO-C201 article’s design approval.

2.2.1 External Aiding Source Performance. When the AHRS requires an external aiding source, ensure the aiding source installed in the aircraft provides the appropriate accuracy, integrity, availability, software level and electronic hardware design assurance.

2.2.2 External Aiding Source Annunciations. The applicant should determine how an external aiding source failure and annunciation affects AHRS performance. Conduct ground and flight testing as necessary to ensure appropriateness of the annunciation and pilot action. Any annunciations should be operationally relevant to minimize flightcrew workload; should be clear, unambiguous and timely; should only be indicated while the condition exists; should be consistently located in a specific area of the electronic display; and be located in the flightcrew’s primary field of view when immediate flightcrew awareness is required. If testing is not possible, provide an analysis to ensure the appropriate action occurs with degradation or failure of the external aiding source. For example, if the AHRS disables the attitude output or switches modes when the aiding source fails, as part of the §§23.1309, 25.1309, 27.1309, or 29.1309 safety analysis, ensure the AHRS acts per design when the aiding source is intentionally disabled.

2.3 GNSS Aiding. GNSS refers to all types of positioning satellites which provide autonomous geo-spatial positioning. Common GNSS systems include, but are not limited to, the navigation signal timing and ranging (NAVSTAR) global positioning system (GPS) (U.S.), globalnaya navigatsionnaya sputnikovaya sistema (GLONASS) (Russian) and Galileo (Europe). GNSS velocity data can be used to compute longitudinal accelerations to help eliminate errors.

2.3.1 GNSS Qualification: When interfacing the AHRS to an external GNSS, ensure the external GNSS provides the needed inputs with the appropriate accuracy, integrity, availability, and software and hardware design assurance.

2.3.1.1 When interfacing with an external GNSS, ensure the external GNSS is qualified to the standards of any revision of:

a) TSO-C145d, Airborne Navigation Sensors Using the Global Positioning System Augmented by the Satellite Based Augmentation System;

b) TSO-C146d, Stand-Alone Airborne Navigation Equipment Using the Global Positioning System Augmented by the Satellite Based Augmentation System; or

c) TSO-C196b, Airborne Supplemental Navigation Sensors for Global Positioning System Equipment using Aircraft-Based Augmentation.

2.3.1.2 This AC does not address AHRS interface to TSO-C129a, Airborne Supplemental Navigation Equipment Using the Global Positioning System (GPS), since this TSO design standard may not provide sufficient availability in high interference environments.

2.3.2 GNSS Velocity Accuracy. If you use velocity accuracy from a GNSS position source, you should ensure the GNSS source data meets the minimum velocity accuracy requirement prescribed by the AHRS installation. GNSS position sources are not required to pass velocity accuracy tests to receive TSO authorization. One means to verify this performance is to ensure the GNSS source passes the velocity accuracy tests prescribed in AC 20-138D, Airworthiness Approval of Positioning and Navigation Systems or subsequent revisions. Typically, the GNSS source equipment manufacturer will accomplish these GNSS tests.

2.3.3 GNSS Faults. It is possible for some GNSS articles to output erroneous position and velocity data after the data is flagged invalid. Review the GNSS specifications to determine if this condition can occur, and if the AHRS detects the annunciated GNSS fault, the AHRS should cease using erroneous GNSS data. Analysis may be used as a means of compliance.

2.4 ADC Aiding. ADC information helps correct attitude pitch and bank angle errors. Ensure AHRS interfaces to an external ADC are qualified, such as any revision of TSO-C106, Air Data Computer, and provides the needed inputs with the appropriate accuracy, integrity, availability, and software and hardware design assurance.

2.5 Pitot Tube Airspeed Sensor Aiding. Pitot data information helps correct attitude pitch and bank angle error introduced by aircraft acceleration. It may directly interface with the AHRS. It is typically used for low velocity and non-complex velocity aircraft profiles. When interfacing the AHRS, ensure information is from a certified aircraft source (for example, TSO-C16, Electrically Heated Pitot and Pitot Static Tubes), and provides the needed inputs with the appropriate accuracy, integrity, availability, and software and hardware design assurance. For more complex velocities, the interface with an ADC may be necessary. Also see Rotorcraft Considerations in Section 5.5

2.6 Magnetic Aiding. When interfacing a magnetic sensor, ensure the sensor’s location is selected to avoid interference from the aircraft structure and systems. For interference associated with known aircraft magnetic anomalies, a compensator may be required to ensure accurate magnetic heading information. Ensure continuous operation of all heading instruments in all foreseeable operating conditions.

3. DEGRADED MODE. TSO-C201 provides allowances for an optional degraded mode to provide basic attitude performance when the AHRS has a partial failure or loses an aiding source. This mode is intended to allow an operator, even under instrument meteorological conditions (IMC), to maintain positive control of the aircraft. RTCA DO-334, Minimum Operational Performance Standards (MOPS) for Solid-State Strapdown Attitude and Heading Reference Systems (AHRS), indicates the degraded mode can support cruise flight, climbs, descents, holding, and instrument approaches. However, the degraded mode may not be acceptable for autopilot operation or certain flight procedures. Evaluate the degraded mode during the airworthiness certification to ensure suitability of the design and operation. Refer to the AHRS manufacturer’s installation manual for specific information regarding AHRS operating modes and equipment performance.

3.1 Degraded Mode Suitability. Determine if the degraded mode performance is acceptable for the intended aircraft and mode of operation in accordance with §§ 23.1301, 25.1301, 27.1301, or 29.1301. Degraded mode may be used on any aircraft type, for primary and secondary attitude sources; however, the TSO-C201 degraded mode is intended for smaller lower performance aircraft, such as part 23 and “non-appendix B” part 27 aircraft, which are typically certificated for one pilot and thus do not have two primary attitude systems installed. The degraded mode provides an alternative to a total loss of primary attitude in an aircraft with a single primary attitude system. In aircraft certificated for two pilot operations, use of the second primary attitude system is the preferred operating method when the first primary attitude system fails or degrades. Do not use degraded mode as a basis to reduce the required number of attitude instruments in an aircraft. If the AHRS installation manual requires flight envelope or time limitations for the degraded mode, insure those limitations are incorporated in the flight manual. The degraded mode is for abnormal conditions and should not be enabled while on the ground, either during initial system start-up or after engine start.

3.2 Degraded Mode Testing. There are two types of degraded mode triggers in AHRS equipment. One can be evaluated in-flight and the other cannot.

3.2.1 For initial AHRS installations, where the degraded mode can be disabled in-flight, such as circuit breaker pull, then the degraded mode should be evaluated through flight testing.

3.2.2 For initial AHRS installations, where the degraded mode cannot be evaluated in-flight, such as accelerometer degradation, then the applicant may use analysis or simulation. Testing should include pilot workload, acceptability of degraded mode through normal instrument flight rules (IFR) maneuvers, including climbs, descents, standard rate turns, and instrument approaches. Testing should also evaluate any effects on the flightcrew’s ability to control the aircraft in flight.

3.2.3 Follow-on installations should demonstrate degraded mode performance for unique aircraft flight envelopes or operating conditions. Applicants using analysis to comply with §§23.1309, 25.1309, 27.1309, 29.1309 and 25.1523 and appendix D to part25 should ensure the degraded mode will safely perform its intended function and will not significantly affect pilot workload or aircraft operation. This analysis should also take into account any effects on the flightcrew’s ability to control the aircraft in flight. In either case, the airplane/rotorcraft flight manual supplement (A/RFMS) should include the degraded mode performance characteristics and limitations.

3.3 Other System Interfaces. The degraded mode performance was defined to support primary attitude, heading, turn rate, and slip-skid indications. Evaluate the suitability of the degraded mode performance for other applications, as it may not be sufficient for higher performance applications, such as an autopilot, head-up display (HUD), or a synthetic vision system (SVS) display. If the analysis shows the degraded mode is not sufficient for other aircraft applications, ensure the degraded mode does not drive those particular aircraft applications.

3.4 Operating Instructions. Ensure the appropriate A/RFMS or applicable operating instructions are updated with a description of the degraded mode, the annunciations provided in degraded mode, and instructions for operating the aircraft. The operating instructions should also indicate which system applications will be lost (e.g., autopilot) and the limitations on types of maneuvers or operations which can be accomplished in degraded mode.

4. TSO-C201 CATEGORIZATIONS AND APPLICATIONS. AHRS, as a minimum, provides attitude information to pilots and/or aircraft. It may also provide heading, turn and slip and other information including acceleration, vertical speed, angular rates, lateral velocity, track data and position. TSO-C201 AHRS articles will typically be identified with a six digit category string. The first two letters define the attitude accuracy, the third and fourth letters define the heading accuracy and availability, and the fifth and sixth letters define the turn and slip capability. For example, the category string A4H4T3 denotes a dynamic attitude accuracy of 2.5º, dynamic heading accuracy of 6^° with magnetic slaving, and turn rate and slip information is provided. It is possible the AHRS will

have different category strings for different modes of operation. Refer to RTCA DO-334, section 2.2 for descriptions of the attitude, heading and turn and slip categories.

4.1 Attitude Category and Application. The attitude categories, A1 through A5, primarily pertain to the accuracy of the AHRS attitude output. All five categories are suitable to drive basic attitude indicators. Some applications, such as HUD and integration of autopilot, may require the higher accuracy categories. Refer to the interfacing systems attitude performance and airworthiness requirements and ensure your AHRS installation meets those requirements.

4.2 Heading Category and Application. There are eleven (11) potential heading categories for TSO-C201 articles, all of which articulate the accuracy of the heading information and its source. The H1 system uses a non-magnetic heading determination (e.g., a gyrocompassing system), the H2 through H5 systems are magnetically slaved (e.g., to a flux valve or magnetometer), and the H6 through H11 categories operate in directional gyro (DG) mode. All heading categories are suitable to drive basic heading indicators; however, categories H10 and H11 are for short-term use when magnetic anomalies exist. Some applications, such as enhanced flight vision systems (EFVS) and integration of the flight management system (FMS) may require higher accuracy categories. Refer to the interfacing systems heading performance and airworthiness requirements and ensure your AHRS installation meets those requirements.

4.3 Turn and Slip Category Application. The seven (7) turn and slip categories, T1 through T7 relate to the availability of turn, bank angle, slip and skid information. Refer to the interfacing systems of turn, bank angle, slip and skid performance and airworthiness requirements and ensure your installation meets those requirements.

4.4 Other AHRS Information for Other Applications. AHRS articles can also provide other features such as acceleration, vertical velocity, angular rates, magnetic wind direction, ground speed, magnetic track angle, and velocity. TSO-C201 does not provide performance requirements for this data, so ensure the AHRS data is appropriate for the intended applications.</context>

## 结论

不能仅凭铝结构固定翼飞机上已有的批准与鉴定数据直接外推到复合材料旋翼机。AC 20-181 的适用对象是申请 TC、ATC、STC 或 ASTC 的 TSO-C201 AHRS 安装批准<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="560e50a3-face-4bdf-a9a8-0e97955dd9ff" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" />，其补充指导正是针对**安装层面**需要评估的四类内容：辅助源、降级模式、TSO-C201 类别与应用、运行考虑<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="d138a1e6-e39f-44ab-8e17-8fb4f2cd32ae" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" />。因此，“环境鉴定已足够、软件、传感器、滤波逻辑均无需重新评估”的假设，与文件中的多项要求不符。

## 需要核实的差异（至少六类）

**1. 旋翼振动频谱与滤波逻辑、软件**

AC 指出，部分 AHRS 难以区分旋翼机运动与安装平台的正常振动频谱<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="ad42789a-7a65-4609-bb52-c3d5dcb2a334" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" />。文中列出的一种被接受的做法是：通过一系列飞行试验测量相应安装区域的振动频谱，再根据数据调整软件逻辑，使系统能区分有效输入与旋翼机正常振动；文中明确说明，这种做法“results in the need to create a specific part number for each installation”<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="876cca22-8883-4c71-aa34-95b4185e07ff" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" />。这与“软件和滤波逻辑不必重新评估”的说法直接冲突，至少对采用该方法的构型成立。

**2. 辅助源与总静压输入**

- 内部辅助源应具备与其用途相适应的精度、完整性、可用性、软件等级与电子硬件设计保证；文中举例：若系统原为通用航空飞机开发而改装于通勤类飞机，则内部辅助源可能需要重新评估<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="ecb42ba7-4e2f-4c54-8278-b206a987adc5" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" />。
- 外部辅助源需满足 2.2.1 的精度、完整性、可用性、软硬件设计保证要求<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="fdc8309b-a5e4-4fef-be23-9371b6c049d3" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" />；外部 GNSS 需符合 TSO-C145d、C146d 或 C196b 的任一版本<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="e5a3c2c8-1a77-47b8-9a8d-a4341a4a993a" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" />；外部 ADC 需合格（如 TSO-C106）<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="a29f8384-f341-4fc4-b2b9-96b58f4d0bcd" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" />；直接接口的 pitot 数据需来自经认证的机载源（如 TSO-C16）<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="82ff318a-2f51-4771-92da-3d0f0657712d" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" />。
- 旋翼机方面：采用 MEMS 并使用 TSO-C16 总静压修正的 AHRS “may not be sufficient for rotorcraft AHRS applications”；低速时总静压数据可能影响姿态解的可靠性与完整性，必要时应演示或评估，若确有影响则可能施加运行限制<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="876cca22-8883-4c71-aa34-95b4185e07ff" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" />。

**3. 磁传感器安装位置与磁干扰**

- 安装磁传感器时，应选择能避免机体结构和系统干扰的位置；对已知机体磁异常可能需要补偿器<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="82ff318a-2f51-4771-92da-3d0f0657712d" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" />。
- 应在代表性环境中评估磁阀或磁强计的安装，以确认磁干扰被最小化<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="6c8ab131-eacc-4599-ace3-bf18b2aac56e" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" />。
- 若安装包含磁阀或磁强计，需评估 DG 模式、人工对准、干扰消失后的快速对准、自动回退等功能；并明确 “A ground or flight test will need to be conducted to evaluate the operational and performance capability”<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="14b18c76-35e6-4465-8579-9a95e2aee732" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" /><kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="6c8ab131-eacc-4599-ace3-bf18b2aac56e" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" />。
- **限定说明**：本次检索到的 AC 文本并未就“复合材料机身”提出专门条款；铝结构基线数据能否代表复合材料安装的磁环境，无法从该文件确定，需另行核实，不能据此断定“无需重评”或“必须重做”。

**4. 适用规章条款与飞机类别、降级模式适用性**

- 降级模式性能是否可接受，需按适用规章条款（§§23.1301、25.1301、27.1301 或 29.1301）判定<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="7d6e410c-ea7d-406c-8b0d-c977170dd823" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" />；相关安全分析与 23.1309、25.1309、27.1309、29.1309 相关<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="560e50a3-face-4bdf-a9a8-0e97955dd9ff" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" /><kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="fdc8309b-a5e4-4fef-be23-9371b6c049d3" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" />。
- TSO-C201 降级模式面向较小、较低性能的飞机，如 Part 23 和“non-appendix B” Part 27 航空器；不得以降级模式为由减少所需姿态仪表数量<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="7d6e410c-ea7d-406c-8b0d-c977170dd823" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" />。
- 类别串需按安装核对（首两字母为姿态精度、第三四字母为航向精度与可用性、第五六字母为转弯与侧滑能力，例如 A4H4T3）；同一 AHRS 在不同工作模式下可能有不同类别串<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="4156512f-c161-45b8-bd7e-272bc09d2b77" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" />；HUD、自动驾驶、EFVS、FMS 等应用可能要求更高类别<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="4156512f-c161-45b8-bd7e-272bc09d2b77" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" /><kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="c5e420da-d11f-4de3-8327-ac9578864902" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" />。

**5. 运行条件差异**

| 运行条件 | 文件要求要点 |
|---|---|
| 极地运行 | 地球磁场异常可导致错误磁航向；若拟在极地运行，申请人应做飞行试验演示，或证明已在“like or similar installation”的飞机上成功演示；后续安装可用仿真或分析；需有真航向选择标识、磁/真航向自动切换的告警，并更新飞行手册<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="0dd3bc99-ab06-4e61-a5ec-302dd1faf314" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" /><kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="14b18c76-35e6-4465-8579-9a95e2aee732" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" /> |
| 高磁干扰区域 | 航母、高压线、直升机起降平台、埋地钢筋、地面设备等均可造成干扰；需评估补偿功能与对通电、初始对准、起飞着陆的影响，并在飞行手册/POH 中加入说明<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="14b18c76-35e6-4465-8579-9a95e2aee732" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" /><kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="6c8ab131-eacc-4599-ace3-bf18b2aac56e" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" /> |
| 低功率/低电压 | 需评估低功率发动机设置及可能伴随的低电压是否影响 AHRS 性能，并将限制写入 A/RFMS 或 POH<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="6c8ab131-eacc-4599-ace3-bf18b2aac56e" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" /> |
| 风速修正敏感性 | 使用风修正的 AHRS 在热带或极地急流 18,000–40,000 ft MSL 区域、以及接近失速的低速大顶风条件下需确保可运行；若无法进行独特风场试验，应提供分析并写入限制<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="ad42789a-7a65-4609-bb52-c3d5dcb2a334" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" /> |

**6. 文件与逐安装批准**

A/RFMS 或 POH 需加入降级模式描述、相应告警、可执行操纵说明、将失去的功能（如自动驾驶）及机动限制<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="e6731b2d-1a5f-4072-b3db-1232e2cdb3b3" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" /><kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="e6a16267-d0c8-4630-9d83-4f162fe0b5e5" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" />；快速对准、人工与自动回退模式的操作说明及磁干扰提示也需写入飞行手册或 POH<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="6c8ab131-eacc-4599-ace3-bf18b2aac56e" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" />。

## 不能仅靠共用基线数据推进的情形

1. 无法提供“like or similar installation”的既往飞行试验证据（如极地运行演示）<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="0dd3bc99-ab06-4e61-a5ec-302dd1faf314" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" />。
2. 采用振动频谱法时，软件逻辑需按安装调整并可能需要**每个安装专用件号**<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="876cca22-8883-4c71-aa34-95b4185e07ff" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" />。
3. 后续（follow-on）安装存在独特飞行包线或运行条件时，应演示降级模式性能<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="e6731b2d-1a5f-4072-b3db-1232e2cdb3b3" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" />。
4. 降级模式可在飞行中触发（如拔出跳开关）时，应通过飞行试验评估<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="e6731b2d-1a5f-4072-b3db-1232e2cdb3b3" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" />。
5. 磁干扰相关功能（DG 模式、人工/快速对准、自动回退）的操行与性能能力，需地面或飞行试验<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="6c8ab131-eacc-4599-ace3-bf18b2aac56e" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" />。
6. 低速时总静压数据可能影响姿态解，需演示或评估，必要时施加运行限制<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="876cca22-8883-4c71-aa34-95b4185e07ff" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" />。
7. 无法进行独特风场试验时，需以分析证明无不利安全问题并在 A/RFMS 中写入限制<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="ad42789a-7a65-4609-bb52-c3d5dcb2a334" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" />。
8. 外部辅助源失效告警与机组动作的适当性，必要时应做地面和飞行试验；无法试验时须提供分析<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="fdc8309b-a5e4-4fef-be23-9371b6c049d3" kb_id="9551ee52-e85f-46f2-b85b-4454b390c84c" />。

## 无法从现有资料确定的事项

本次检索内容未涉及具体环境鉴定标准（如 DO-160 的试验类别、试验剖面）的条款，也未涉及复合材料结构对磁传感器影响的具体判据。因此，“既有环境鉴定是否足够”以及“复合材料机体是否需要专门的磁环境验证”不能依据本文件得出肯定结论，应由适用的环境鉴定与安装评估资料另行确认；本回答不推断相关数值或试验项目。

5. OPERATIONAL CONSIDERATIONS.

5.1 Polar Operations. The polar region environment is defined as the area beginning at 5^° to 30º latitude from the pole, depending on location, and extending to either the north or south pole. Anomalies with the earth’s magnetic field in the polar region can provide erroneous magnetic heading indications. Aircraft will typically use true heading information when flying in Polar Regions.

5.1.1 If the AHRS article is installed on aircraft intended to operate in the Polar Regions, the applicant should conduct a flight test demonstration to show proper operation for new AHRS articles or show previous successful flight test demonstration in an aircraft of like or similar installation. If the AHRS article was flight tested under the combined TSO-STC process, then the applicant should ensure the aircraft complies with the TSO article installation limitations and STC. Simulation testing and/or analysis are acceptable methods of compliance for follow-on installations.

5.1.2 Ensure a means is provided to identify when true heading is selected, such as information on the display or marking on a control panel.

5.1.3 Evaluate any automatic switching from magnetic to true heading or vice versa while entering and exiting Polar Regions. If the automatic switching between magnetic/true heading is not sufficiently self-evident, a suitable alerting or other annunciation should accompany the automatic switching.

5.1.4 Ensure the flight manual is updated with any unique procedures for landing, departing and flying the aircraft in Polar Regions.

5.1.5 If AHRS performance degrades in the polar region a visual indication should be provided to the flightcrew. An aural annunciation may be provided as well, depending on the specific system design and overall flight deck philosophy. Any annunciation should be clear, unambiguous, timely and attention getting; should only be indicated while the condition exists; should be consistently located in a specific area of the electronic display; and be located in the flight crew’s primary field of view when immediate flightcrew awareness is required.

5.1.6 If the AHRS is not qualified to fly in the polar region, ensure the A/RFMS includes the appropriate limitations.

5.2 Areas of High Magnetic Disturbances. High magnetic disturbance areas can be caused by aircraft carriers, power lines, elevated helicopter-landing platforms, buried concrete steel reinforcing bars, ground equipment in close proximity to the aircraft, or a myriad of other conditions.

5.2.1 When an AHRS installation includes a flux valve or magnetometer, evaluate the functionalities below used to compensate for magnetic disturbance if they are included with the AHRS installation.

a) A DG mode which temporarily deactivates the flux valve or magnetometer;

b) A manual alignment mode allowing the pilot to manually align the affected system in an area away from the magnetic interference;

c) Rapid alignment capability once the magnetic interference is gone; or,

d) Automatic reversion. Automatic reversion may be required for those installations where Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) systems and oil drilling platforms are normal landing areas to meet the applicable safety requirements. A timed, free gyro mode (DG or similar) may be acceptable. Ensure the system is available at landing and initial alignment or allows an alternate short-term un-slaved mode with a set-heading alignment capability. A ground or flight test will need to be conducted to evaluate the operational and performance capability.

5.2.2 Evaluate the installation of the flux valve or magnetometer in a representative environment to ensure magnetic disturbances are minimized.

5.2.3 Evaluate the effects of power-up, initial alignment, take offs, and landings from areas of high magnetic disturbance, when applicable.

5.2.4 Ensure instructions for the rapid alignment, manual and automatic reversion modes are added to the flight manual or pilot’s operating handbook (POH).

5.2.5 Ensure instructions are added to the flight manual or POH identifying the potential for magnetic disturbances, when applicable.

5.3 Low Power Setting. Evaluate low power engine settings and possible associated low voltage conditions to determine if they affect AHRS performance. This evaluation is necessary because the FAA has identified concerns with low power settings causing fluctuations and erroneous orientations of heading and attitude displays. Ensure any resulting limitations are addressed in the A/RFMS or POH.

5.4 Wind Speeds. Some AHRS use wind calculations to correct the heading information. Depending on the magnetic variation and algorithms, some are more sensitive to changes in wind speed and direction than others. For aircraft using these corrections and flying in or around tropical areas or polar jet streams between 18,000 ft - 40,000 ft Mean Sea Level (MSL), ensure AHRS operability for these regimes. Also, evaluate these systems at lower aircraft speeds near stall with high headwind components. If testing with the unique wind dynamics is not possible, then the installer should provide some means of analysis to ensure the system is capable of operating with no adverse safety issues and provide any limitations in the A/RFMS. If the AHRS integrates with a windshear system, verify operational capability and limitations.

5.5 Rotorcraft Considerations. Some AHRS have a difficult time distinguishing between rotorcraft movement and the normal vibration spectrum of the platform to which it is mounted. Manufacturers of this technology have different approaches on how to “filter” these inputs so an accurate attitude solution can be derived. Other solutions are possible, but listed are a few accepted approaches.

a) One approach relies on surveying the vibration spectrum of the applicable installation area by conducting a series of flight test evaluations. Based on data obtained during these flight tests, adjustments are made to the software logic to allow the system to adequately distinguish valid from invalid inputs (i.e., those resulting from the rotorcraft’s normal vibration). This approach results in the need to create a specific part number for each installation.

b)	 Another approach relies on the use of GNSS and vector data to “stabilize and correct” the attitude solution.

d)	 A third approach relies on the use of pitot static information to help correct and stabilize the accelerometer derived attitude solution. AHRS designed with MEMS technology using TSO-C16 pitot/static corrections, may not be sufficient for rotorcraft AHRS applications. Operational rotorcraft maneuvers differ in performance from fixed wing aircraft, because they involve roll, pitch, and yaw rates coupled with translations in all directions to a stationary hover. For rotorcraft applications, ensure the pitot system, if used, provides the needed inputs with the appropriate accuracy, integrity, and availability. If necessary, demonstrate or evaluate the performance of the pitot system especially in low speeds, where pitot/static data may affect the reliability and integrity of the attitude solution. If it does affect the attitude solution, a limitation on the operation may apply.

Source image on page 8; no OCR transcription available.

James D. Seipel

Acting Manager, Design, Manufacturing, &

Airworthiness Division

Aircraft Certification Service

U.S. Department of Transportation Federal Aviation Administration

Advisory Circular

Subject: AIRWORTHINESS APPROVAL OF ATTITUDE HEADING REFERENCE SYSTEM (AHRS) EQUIPMENT

Date: 4/7/14

AC No: 20-181

Initiated By: AIR-130

1. GENERAL INFORMATION.

1.1 Purpose. This advisory circular (AC) supplements existing airworthiness approval guidance for attitude heading reference system (AHRS) articles approved under technical standard order (TSO)-C201, Attitude Heading Reference System, or later revisions. TSO-C201 includes performance standards for non-gimbaled attitude, heading, and turn and slip systems. Appendix A contains a list of acronyms. Appendix B explains where to obtain reference documents. Refer to the latest revision of following list of ACs to complete the aircraft type specific primary or stand-by flight instrument airworthiness certification process:

a)	 AC 20-167, Airworthiness Approval of Enhanced Vision Systems, Synthetic Vision Systems, Combined Vision Systems, and Enhanced Flight Vision Systems;

b) AC 23-8, Flight Test Guide for Certification of Part 23 Airplanes;

c) AC 23-17, Systems and Equipment Guide for Certification of Part 23 Airplane and Airships;

d) AC 23.1309-1, System Safety Analysis and Assessment for Part 23 Airplanes;

e) AC 23.1311-1, Installation of Electronic Displays in Part 23 Airplanes;

f) AC 25-7, Flight Test Guidance for Part 25 Airplanes;

g) AC 25-11, Electronic Flight Deck Displays;

h) AC 25.1302-1, Installed Systems and Equipment for Use by the Flightcrew;

i) AC 25.1309-1, System Design and Analysis;

j) AC 25.1322-1, Flightcrew Alerting;

k) AC 25.1329-1, Approval of Flight Guidance Systems;

l) AC 27-1, Certification of Normal Category Rotorcraft; and

m) AC 29-2, Certification of Transport Category Rotorcraft.

1.2 Related CFR Regulations. Title 14 of the Code of Federal Regulations (14 CFR)

a)	 Part 23, §§ 23.1301, .1303, .1309, .1311, .1321, .1322, and .1327.

b)	 Part 25, §§ 25.1301, .1302, .1303, .1309, .1321, .1322, .1327, .1333, .1523 and Appendix D.

c)	 Part 27, §§ 27.1301, .1303, .1309, .1321, .1322, .1327, and Appendix B.

d)	 Part 29, §§ 29.1301, .1303, .1309, .1321, .1322, .1327, .1333, and Appendix B

1.3 Audience. This AC provides guidance for aircraft manufacturers, avionics manufacturers, installation shops, or other applicants seeking airworthiness approval under type certificate (TC), amended type certificate (ATC), supplemental type certificate (STC), or amended supplemental type certificate (ASTC) for TSO-C201 AHRS equipment.

1.4 Background. Manufacturers of attitude (pitch and roll), heading, turn and slip instruments have used TSO-C3, TSO-C4, TSO-C5, and TSO-C6 standards, dating back to 1958. More recently, AHRS based on micro-electro-mechanical systems (MEMS), ring-laser gyros (RLG), fiber optic gyros (FOG), and other technologies, are replacing conventional attitude and heading instruments to increase data performance reliability and accuracy. AHRS provides attitude and heading measurements with both static and dynamic accuracy comparable to traditional gimbaled systems. TSO-C201 does not cancel the older TSOs, but has been written for the non-gimbaled attitude and heading systems. When we published TSO-C201, many airworthiness approval policies existed for primary and stand-by flight instrumentation for each aircraft category type, as listed in Section 1.1. Although comprehensive, those policies do not address certain features included in TSO-C201 which require evaluation at installation. This AC's supplemental guidance addresses four specific areas:

a)	 Aiding Sources;

b)	 Degraded Mode;

c)	 TSO-C201 Categorizations and Applications; and,

d)	 Operational Considerations.

2. AHRS AIDING SOURCES. An AHRS aiding source is an internal or external system which provides additional sensor information to the core strap down attitude heading reference function. Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) and air data computer (ADC) aiding sources are commonly used to identify aircraft accelerations to reduce errors in the attitude function. Flux valves and magnetometers provide magnetic reference for heading functions, and numerous sources can be used for performance monitoring. Some aiding designs only supplement the AHRS functionality, and loss of aiding may only have limited effect on AHRS performance. On other designs, aiding may provide integral information where loss of the aiding source could lead to loss of AHRS functionality.

2.1 Internal Aiding Source Installations. Evaluate internal aiding sources as part of the overall article’s intended function evaluation. The internal aiding source should be qualified as part of the TSO-C201 design approval process. Ensure the aiding source provides the needed inputs with the appropriate accuracy, integrity, availability, and software level and electronic hardware design

assurance for its intended use. For example, if the system was developed for a general aviation aircraft, but will be installed on a commuter aircraft, then the internal aiding source may need to be re-evaluated to ensure the appropriate compatibility with the aircraft’s design architecture and its usage.

2.2 External Aiding Source Installations. This paragraph applies to external aiding sources not qualified as part of the TSO-C201 article’s design approval.

2.2.1 External Aiding Source Performance. When the AHRS requires an external aiding source, ensure the aiding source installed in the aircraft provides the appropriate accuracy, integrity, availability, software level and electronic hardware design assurance.

2.2.2 External Aiding Source Annunciations. The applicant should determine how an external aiding source failure and annunciation affects AHRS performance. Conduct ground and flight testing as necessary to ensure appropriateness of the annunciation and pilot action. Any annunciations should be operationally relevant to minimize flightcrew workload; should be clear, unambiguous and timely; should only be indicated while the condition exists; should be consistently located in a specific area of the electronic display; and be located in the flightcrew’s primary field of view when immediate flightcrew awareness is required. If testing is not possible, provide an analysis to ensure the appropriate action occurs with degradation or failure of the external aiding source. For example, if the AHRS disables the attitude output or switches modes when the aiding source fails, as part of the §§23.1309, 25.1309, 27.1309, or 29.1309 safety analysis, ensure the AHRS acts per design when the aiding source is intentionally disabled.

2.3 GNSS Aiding. GNSS refers to all types of positioning satellites which provide autonomous geo-spatial positioning. Common GNSS systems include, but are not limited to, the navigation signal timing and ranging (NAVSTAR) global positioning system (GPS) (U.S.), globalnaya navigatsionnaya sputnikovaya sistema (GLONASS) (Russian) and Galileo (Europe). GNSS velocity data can be used to compute longitudinal accelerations to help eliminate errors.

2.3.1 GNSS Qualification: When interfacing the AHRS to an external GNSS, ensure the external GNSS provides the needed inputs with the appropriate accuracy, integrity, availability, and software and hardware design assurance.

2.3.1.1 When interfacing with an external GNSS, ensure the external GNSS is qualified to the standards of any revision of:

a) TSO-C145d, Airborne Navigation Sensors Using the Global Positioning System Augmented by the Satellite Based Augmentation System;

b) TSO-C146d, Stand-Alone Airborne Navigation Equipment Using the Global Positioning System Augmented by the Satellite Based Augmentation System; or

c) TSO-C196b, Airborne Supplemental Navigation Sensors for Global Positioning System Equipment using Aircraft-Based Augmentation.

2.3.1.2 This AC does not address AHRS interface to TSO-C129a, Airborne Supplemental Navigation Equipment Using the Global Positioning System (GPS), since this TSO design standard may not provide sufficient availability in high interference environments.

2.3.2 GNSS Velocity Accuracy. If you use velocity accuracy from a GNSS position source, you should ensure the GNSS source data meets the minimum velocity accuracy requirement prescribed by the AHRS installation. GNSS position sources are not required to pass velocity accuracy tests to receive TSO authorization. One means to verify this performance is to ensure the GNSS source passes the velocity accuracy tests prescribed in AC 20-138D, Airworthiness Approval of Positioning and Navigation Systems or subsequent revisions. Typically, the GNSS source equipment manufacturer will accomplish these GNSS tests.

2.3.3 GNSS Faults. It is possible for some GNSS articles to output erroneous position and velocity data after the data is flagged invalid. Review the GNSS specifications to determine if this condition can occur, and if the AHRS detects the annunciated GNSS fault, the AHRS should cease using erroneous GNSS data. Analysis may be used as a means of compliance.

2.4 ADC Aiding. ADC information helps correct attitude pitch and bank angle errors. Ensure AHRS interfaces to an external ADC are qualified, such as any revision of TSO-C106, Air Data Computer, and provides the needed inputs with the appropriate accuracy, integrity, availability, and software and hardware design assurance.

2.5 Pitot Tube Airspeed Sensor Aiding. Pitot data information helps correct attitude pitch and bank angle error introduced by aircraft acceleration. It may directly interface with the AHRS. It is typically used for low velocity and non-complex velocity aircraft profiles. When interfacing the AHRS, ensure information is from a certified aircraft source (for example, TSO-C16, Electrically Heated Pitot and Pitot Static Tubes), and provides the needed inputs with the appropriate accuracy, integrity, availability, and software and hardware design assurance. For more complex velocities, the interface with an ADC may be necessary. Also see Rotorcraft Considerations in Section 5.5

2.6 Magnetic Aiding. When interfacing a magnetic sensor, ensure the sensor’s location is selected to avoid interference from the aircraft structure and systems. For interference associated with known aircraft magnetic anomalies, a compensator may be required to ensure accurate magnetic heading information. Ensure continuous operation of all heading instruments in all foreseeable operating conditions.

3. DEGRADED MODE. TSO-C201 provides allowances for an optional degraded mode to provide basic attitude performance when the AHRS has a partial failure or loses an aiding source. This mode is intended to allow an operator, even under instrument meteorological conditions (IMC), to maintain positive control of the aircraft. RTCA DO-334, Minimum Operational Performance Standards (MOPS) for Solid-State Strapdown Attitude and Heading Reference Systems (AHRS), indicates the degraded mode can support cruise flight, climbs, descents, holding, and instrument approaches. However, the degraded mode may not be acceptable for autopilot operation or certain flight procedures. Evaluate the degraded mode during the airworthiness certification to ensure suitability of the design and operation. Refer to the AHRS manufacturer’s installation manual for specific information regarding AHRS operating modes and equipment performance.

3.1 Degraded Mode Suitability. Determine if the degraded mode performance is acceptable for the intended aircraft and mode of operation in accordance with §§ 23.1301, 25.1301, 27.1301, or 29.1301. Degraded mode may be used on any aircraft type, for primary and secondary attitude sources; however, the TSO-C201 degraded mode is intended for smaller lower performance aircraft, such as part 23 and “non-appendix B” part 27 aircraft, which are typically certificated for one pilot and thus do not have two primary attitude systems installed. The degraded mode provides an alternative to a total loss of primary attitude in an aircraft with a single primary attitude system. In aircraft certificated for two pilot operations, use of the second primary attitude system is the preferred operating method when the first primary attitude system fails or degrades. Do not use degraded mode as a basis to reduce the required number of attitude instruments in an aircraft. If the AHRS installation manual requires flight envelope or time limitations for the degraded mode, insure those limitations are incorporated in the flight manual. The degraded mode is for abnormal conditions and should not be enabled while on the ground, either during initial system start-up or after engine start.

3.2 Degraded Mode Testing. There are two types of degraded mode triggers in AHRS equipment. One can be evaluated in-flight and the other cannot.

3.2.1 For initial AHRS installations, where the degraded mode can be disabled in-flight, such as circuit breaker pull, then the degraded mode should be evaluated through flight testing.

3.2.2 For initial AHRS installations, where the degraded mode cannot be evaluated in-flight, such as accelerometer degradation, then the applicant may use analysis or simulation. Testing should include pilot workload, acceptability of degraded mode through normal instrument flight rules (IFR) maneuvers, including climbs, descents, standard rate turns, and instrument approaches. Testing should also evaluate any effects on the flightcrew’s ability to control the aircraft in flight.

3.2.3 Follow-on installations should demonstrate degraded mode performance for unique aircraft flight envelopes or operating conditions. Applicants using analysis to comply with §§23.1309, 25.1309, 27.1309, 29.1309 and 25.1523 and appendix D to part25 should ensure the degraded mode will safely perform its intended function and will not significantly affect pilot workload or aircraft operation. This analysis should also take into account any effects on the flightcrew’s ability to control the aircraft in flight. In either case, the airplane/rotorcraft flight manual supplement (A/RFMS) should include the degraded mode performance characteristics and limitations.

3.3 Other System Interfaces. The degraded mode performance was defined to support primary attitude, heading, turn rate, and slip-skid indications. Evaluate the suitability of the degraded mode performance for other applications, as it may not be sufficient for higher performance applications, such as an autopilot, head-up display (HUD), or a synthetic vision system (SVS) display. If the analysis shows the degraded mode is not sufficient for other aircraft applications, ensure the degraded mode does not drive those particular aircraft applications.

3.4 Operating Instructions. Ensure the appropriate A/RFMS or applicable operating instructions are updated with a description of the degraded mode, the annunciations provided in degraded mode, and instructions for operating the aircraft. The operating instructions should also indicate which system applications will be lost (e.g., autopilot) and the limitations on types of maneuvers or operations which can be accomplished in degraded mode.

4. TSO-C201 CATEGORIZATIONS AND APPLICATIONS. AHRS, as a minimum, provides attitude information to pilots and/or aircraft. It may also provide heading, turn and slip and other information including acceleration, vertical speed, angular rates, lateral velocity, track data and position. TSO-C201 AHRS articles will typically be identified with a six digit category string. The first two letters define the attitude accuracy, the third and fourth letters define the heading accuracy and availability, and the fifth and sixth letters define the turn and slip capability. For example, the category string A4H4T3 denotes a dynamic attitude accuracy of 2.5º, dynamic heading accuracy of 6^° with magnetic slaving, and turn rate and slip information is provided. It is possible the AHRS will

have different category strings for different modes of operation. Refer to RTCA DO-334, section 2.2 for descriptions of the attitude, heading and turn and slip categories.

4.1 Attitude Category and Application. The attitude categories, A1 through A5, primarily pertain to the accuracy of the AHRS attitude output. All five categories are suitable to drive basic attitude indicators. Some applications, such as HUD and integration of autopilot, may require the higher accuracy categories. Refer to the interfacing systems attitude performance and airworthiness requirements and ensure your AHRS installation meets those requirements.

4.2 Heading Category and Application. There are eleven (11) potential heading categories for TSO-C201 articles, all of which articulate the accuracy of the heading information and its source. The H1 system uses a non-magnetic heading determination (e.g., a gyrocompassing system), the H2 through H5 systems are magnetically slaved (e.g., to a flux valve or magnetometer), and the H6 through H11 categories operate in directional gyro (DG) mode. All heading categories are suitable to drive basic heading indicators; however, categories H10 and H11 are for short-term use when magnetic anomalies exist. Some applications, such as enhanced flight vision systems (EFVS) and integration of the flight management system (FMS) may require higher accuracy categories. Refer to the interfacing systems heading performance and airworthiness requirements and ensure your AHRS installation meets those requirements.

4.3 Turn and Slip Category Application. The seven (7) turn and slip categories, T1 through T7 relate to the availability of turn, bank angle, slip and skid information. Refer to the interfacing systems of turn, bank angle, slip and skid performance and airworthiness requirements and ensure your installation meets those requirements.

4.4 Other AHRS Information for Other Applications. AHRS articles can also provide other features such as acceleration, vertical velocity, angular rates, magnetic wind direction, ground speed, magnetic track angle, and velocity. TSO-C201 does not provide performance requirements for this data, so ensure the AHRS data is appropriate for the intended applications.

agent_steps.reasoning_content:
The user asks: an AHRS already approved on aluminum-structure airplanes is proposed for multi-model approval, extended to composite rotorcraft. Applicant believes existing environmental qualification is sufficient, software, sensors, and filtering logic need not be re-evaluated. Need to identify at least four categories of differences to verify, and explain when one cannot proceed solely on shared baseline data.

Key evidence: AC 20-181, section 5.5 Rotorcraft Considerations (c4, c5), 2.6 Magnetic Aiding (c16), 2.1 Internal aiding (c12), 2.2/2.3 GNSS (c13, c14, c15), 2.4 ADC, 2.5 pitot (c16), 5.2 magnetic disturbances (c2, c3), 5.3 low power setting, 5.4 wind speeds, 5.1 polar (c1), degraded mode (c17-c20), categorizations (c21-c23).

Four+ categories:
1. 旋翼振动频谱与滤波逻辑/软件调整 — 5.5 a): flight test survey vibration spectrum, adjust software logic; results in specific part number per installation. So applicant's claim that software/filter logic need not be re-evaluated contradicts guidance — for vibration-spectrum approach, software logic adjustments and specific part number may be needed. Also b) GNSS/vector aiding, d) pitot static; MEMS with TSO-C16 pitot/static corrections may not be sufficient for rotorcraft; low speed pitot performance; limitations may apply.
2. 磁传感器安装与机体结构（复合材料 vs 铝）— 2.6 magnetic sensor location to avoid interference from aircraft structure and systems; compensator may be required. 5.2.2 evaluate flux valve/magnetometer installation in representative environment; magnetic disturbance compensation functions (DG mode, manual alignment, rapid alignment, automatic reversion). Note: the AC does not explicitly say composite structure changes magnetic interference — careful. It says ensure sensor location selected to avoid interference from aircraft structure and systems; evaluate installation in representative environment. I should not assert that composite changes magnetic characteristics (that's a deduction); I can note the AC requires evaluation of location/interference in representative environment, and structure change means the prior aluminum baseline may not represent it — but label as deduction? Better: quote the requirement and say the AC requires evaluation in a representative environment; whether prior aluminum data represents composite installation is not established by the AC — needs verification.

## 结论

申请人的假设不成立。AC 20-181 本身就把“安装层面需要额外评估”的内容限定为四类：辅助源、降级模式、TSO-C201 分类与应用、运行考虑，并说明既有政策“do not address certain features included in TSO-C201 which require evaluation at installation”<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="4467d543-a5f8-4f2a-bd49-326efc910a47" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" />。该 AC 面向申请 TC/ATC/STC/ASTC 的安装批准申请人<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="fdc2667a-fd34-467f-aedd-faaebb1013ea" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" />，而第 5.5 节专门针对旋翼机，直接涉及“软件逻辑调整”和“每一安装专用件号”<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="74448d33-db11-4170-8962-ef0f25bf76ce" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" />。因此，“既有环境鉴定足够、软件、传感器与滤波逻辑均无需重评”与文件中的多项要求冲突。

> 说明：AC 属咨询通告，条文中的“should/ensure”为可接受符合性方法，非 CFR 强制条文；但一旦以该 AC 作为符合性方法，就应按其适用条款执行，且适用性需结合各自审定基础确认。

**关于“复合材料”的界限**：AC 20-181 的文本只要求“避免机体结构与系统的干扰”“在代表性环境中评估”，未就复合材料机身给出专门判据。因此，铝结构飞机上的数据能否代表复合材料安装的磁环境与结构耦合，不能由该文件直接判定；申请人须另行论证，而不是默认沿用。另可参考 AC 20-180 的提示：某个型号若存在独特且复杂的安装问题（原文举例即“如何在复合材料结构上正确穿孔压力容器”），宜考虑以既有基线数据加补充要求申请新的非 AML 的 STC<kb doc="AC_20-180.pdf" chunk_id="62d1c2dc-c25e-443d-a05e-5c0993328432" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" />。

2. **基线数据必须逐型号确立适用性，且每个型号都要表明符合 §21.20**（型号设计、证实性数据、飞行手册补充），“不是一揽子批准”<kb doc="AC_20-180.pdf" chunk_id="9259d265-e30d-414a-ad08-7f80edd1da54" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" /><kb doc="AC_20-180.pdf" chunk_id="3705aad7-9fcf-4093-9520-acd528861605" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" />。
3. **振动频谱法本身会产生“每一安装专用件号”**，这从根本上否定了单一软件/滤波构型直接套用到新安装<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="74448d33-db11-4170-8962-ef0f25bf76ce" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" />。
4. **需要地面或飞行试验才能确认的项目**：磁干扰补偿功能（DG、人工/快速对准、自动回退）的运行与性能能力<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="2e33913b-1778-462b-9890-e0d0dcefba1f" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" />；外部辅助源失效告警与机组动作的适当性（无法试验时才以分析替代）<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="7b6687b0-fc67-40e8-88b7-0355dadc811e" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" />。
5. **新件极地运行**需飞行试验演示，或证明已在“like or similar installation”的飞机上成功演示；仅 follow-on（后续）安装才可用仿真/分析<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="219981f0-0ff8-49e0-9658-110f74620ec2" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" />。
6. **可在飞行中禁用的降级模式**应通过飞行试验评估；后续安装还须针对独特飞行包线或运行条件演示降级模式性能<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="770bf72f-942a-4298-acfe-264546d3acf9" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" />。
7. **低速皮托/静压数据影响姿态解算**时须演示或评估，并可能施加运行限制<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="74448d33-db11-4170-8962-ef0f25bf76ce" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" />。
8. **直接控制航空器的系统可能不适合 AML-STC**：涉及控制输入的安装（原文以自动驾驶为例）“may require careful design, installation, and testing on each proposed model regardless of baseline data shared between them”；若 AHRS 输出参与自动驾驶或控制回路，这一点尤其要评估<kb doc="AC_20-180.pdf" chunk_id="2441846f-0493-4683-b94c-52cfa4f7b2b2" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" />。
9. **可接受的替代路径**（并非一律重做）：独特风场无法试验时，可由安装方提供分析并写入 A/RFMS 限制<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="507765c2-c62c-48d4-aea4-e23f94596b16" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" />；不可在飞行中评估的降级模式可用分析或仿真，但须覆盖飞行员工作负荷与常规 IFR 机动<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="770bf72f-942a-4298-acfe-264546d3acf9" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" />。

## 无法从现有资料确定的事项

- 具体的**环境鉴定**标准与试验剖面（如 DO-160 类别）在 AC 20-181 的检索内容中没有相应条款；因此，“既有环境鉴定是否足够”不能据该文件得出结论，须以适用的环境鉴定与安装评估资料另行核实。
- 复合材料结构对磁传感器精度、结构耦合与振动传递的**具体量化影响**同样未见条款，不能推断，也不能据此默认可共用或必须重做。

相关背景页可参见 [[concept/rotorcraft-ahrs-installation-vibration-filtering|旋翼机AHRS安装与振动滤波]]、[[concept/ahrs-aiding-sources|AHRS辅助源]]、[[concept/high-magnetic-disturbance-areas|高磁干扰区域]]、[[concept/ahrs-degraded-mode|AHRS降级模式]]、[[concept/aml-stc|AML-STC]]。

# Wiki Index

本索引页汇总FAA咨询通告及相关适航批准资料，内容覆盖可充电锂电池、机载激光设备、认证数据保留、姿态航向参考系统、客舱内饰板可燃性测试、AML STC多型号批准和机载气象雷达等主题。页面将随文档新增自动更新。

## Summary (7)

[[summary/17750888-7f2d-42a5-9896-36e1e835687b|AC_20-178.pdf - Summary]] — 本咨询通告[[entity/ac-20-178|AC 20-178]]（2012年6月4日）说明现有客舱内饰板使用新饰面时可接受的[[concept/aircraft-cabin-interior-panel-flammability-testing|飞机客舱内饰板可燃性测试]]与[[concept/surrogate-panel-testing-options|替代板测试方法与五种测试选项]]，并列出相关法规和常见问题。
[[summary/f185e13d-08a9-4ca4-90ea-270b37335cf2|AC_20-179.pdf - Summary]] — 本页总结FAA 2013年[[entity/ac-20-179|AC 20-179 咨询通告]]，涵盖认证数据保留协议、政府记录、适用范围与数据提交要求。
[[summary/68d911e2-3d18-46f0-bcdd-8bf3eb7b5758|AC_20-180.pdf - Summary]] — 本文件为FAA于2013年8月16日发布的[[entity/faa-ac-20-180|AC 20-180]]，说明通过[[concept/aml-stc|批准型号清单补充型号合格证]]进行多型号批准的可接受方法，并附[[entity/sa01157la|SA01157LA]]示例清单。
[[summary/a26c5a50-b9ab-45ca-bb63-ade22f5939f2|AC_20-181.pdf - Summary]] — 本文件为美国联邦航空管理局2014年发布的AC 20-181咨询通告，说明按[[entity/tso-c201-attitude-heading-reference-system|TSO-C201《姿态航向参考系统》技术标准规定]]批准的[[entity/attitude-heading-reference-system|姿态航向参考系统]]设备的适航批准补充指导及极地运行考虑。
[[summary/c5cf4dee-88c4-4a77-983a-35b9963588d8|AC_20-182A.pdf - Summary]] — 本咨询通告提供机载气象雷达系统初始及后续适航批准指导，涵盖气象/地面测绘、前视风切变与湍流探测，并规定测试评估要求。
[[summary/e0166761-78fe-46eb-b323-0225fc5c9e02|AC_20-183.pdf - Summary]] — 本顾问通告说明机载非必需不可见光谱激光设备取得FAA适航批准的一种可接受方法，并列出激光危害分级及第7节安装要求适用性示例。
[[summary/a55aa2ce-d249-4213-a67d-5b8ae36edfb1|AC_20-184.pdf - Summary]] — 本文件是FAA于2015年10月15日发布的咨询通告，提供航空器可充电锂电池及电池系统安装、运行、维护和适航符合性的可接受方法。

## Entity (20)

[[entity/flir|前视红外设备]] — 本页介绍前视红外设备（FLIR）的定义、执法夜间隐蔽监视用途、其配备的激光照射器与测距仪所带来的眼部危害，以及相关波长与损伤机理。
[[entity/lidar|激光雷达]] — 本页依据 AC 20-183 说明激光雷达（LIDAR）的定义、测距原理与用途、激光类别与外部发射等级，以及其不可见光束造成的眼危害与在机载适航安装中的定位。
[[entity/attitude-heading-reference-system|姿态航向参考系统]] — 本页依据 AC 20-181（日期 4/7/14）整理姿态航向参考系统（AHRS）的适航批准要点，涵盖 TSO-C201 辅助源、降级模式、分类应用与极地运行等考虑。
[[entity/reactive-windshear-system|反应式风切变系统]] — 本页依据 AC 20-182A 第 6.4.2 节，说明反应式风切变系统在与机载前视风切变系统共存时的告警配置要求，包括提示告警禁用条件与警告告警保持启用。
[[entity/faa-ac-20-184|FAA咨询通告AC 20-184]] — 本页整理FAA咨询通告AC 20-184（2015年10月15日，AIR-133）的内容，涵盖航空器可充电锂电池与电池系统安装的可接受符合性方法、测试要求、系统安全评估、持续适航文件及维护与运行考虑。
[[entity/ac-20-183|咨询通告20-183]] — 本页介绍美国联邦航空管理局2014年12月15日发布的咨询通告AC 20-183，说明其目的、适用范围、限制及适用对象。
[[entity/faa-aircraft-materials-fire-test-handbook|FAA飞机材料防火测试手册]] — 本页介绍FAA飞机材料防火测试手册（DOT/FAA/AR-00/12），说明其作为14 CFR part 25 Appendix F可接受符合性方法的定位，以及在AC 20-184中对隔热隔音材料防火测试的引用。
[[entity/rtca-do-254|RTCA/DO-254机载电子硬件设计保证指南]] — RTCA/DO-254《机载电子硬件设计保证指南》用于复杂电子硬件的设计保证与适航符合性；FAA AC 20-184第2.6节要求含复杂电子硬件的锂电池硬件符合其最新修订版及AC 20-152。
[[entity/rtca-do-311|RTCA DO-311标准]] — 概述RTCA DO-311标准在FAA AC 20-184中作为大型锂电池可接受符合性方法的定位、适用条件及附录F引用章节。
[[entity/rtca-do-347|RTCA DO-347标准]] — RTCA DO-347是RTCA发布的《Certification Test Guidance for Small and Medium Sized Rechargeable Lithium Batteries and Battery Systems》，FAA AC 20-184（2015-10-15）将其列为小型和中型可充电锂电池及电池系统的可接受符合性方法标准。
[[entity/ac-20-178|AC 20-178咨询通告]] — 本页汇总FAA AC 20-178咨询通告（2012年6月4日）关于飞机客舱内饰板更改后自熄性可燃性测试的适用目的、替代板定义与判定条件、表2五种测试选项、表3问答及偏离与相关出版物。

<content>
# 旋翼机AHRS安装与振动滤波

本页内容整理自 AC 20-181（文件号与日期按原文保留：AC 20-181，4/7/14）。该文件为咨询通告，原文中的“should/ensure”等属指导性表述，不是联邦航空法规（CFR）本身的强制要求；具体项目仍需结合适用审定基础和最新修订文件确认。

旋翼机AHRS安装与振动滤波，涉及AHRS在旋翼机上区分机体运动与正常振动、获得准确姿态解算的安装与验证考虑。原文列出以下处理途径：

a) 一种方法依赖通过一系列飞行试验评估，测量（survey）适用安装区域的振动频谱。基于这些飞行试验获得的数据，对软件逻辑进行调整，使系统能够充分区分有效输入与无效输入（即由旋翼机正常振动引起的输入）。该方法的结果是需要为每一种安装创建特定的件号（part number）。

b) 另一种方法依赖使用 GNSS 和矢量数据对姿态解算进行“稳定和校正”（stabilize and correct）。

d) 第三种方法依赖使用皮托静压信息帮助校正和稳定由加速度计导出的姿态解算。采用 MEMS 技术、使用 TSO-C16 皮托/静压校正设计的 AHRS，可能不足以用于旋翼机 AHRS 应用。旋翼机机动飞行的性能与固定翼飞机不同，因为其涉及滚转、俯仰和偏航角速率，并伴随各方向的平移直至定点悬停。

对于旋翼机应用，应确保皮托系统（如使用）以适当的精度、完整性和可用性提供所需输入。如有必要，应演示或评估皮托系统的性能，特别是在低速下——此时皮托/静压数据可能影响姿态解算的可靠性和完整性。如果确实影响姿态解算，则可能适用运行限制。

## 解析说明

- 给定来源内容中的途径编号为 a)、b)、d)，未出现 c) 项；本页不推断缺失项的内容。
- 文件号与日期“4/7/14”按原文格式保留，未改写为其他日期格式。
- 本页整理的是 AC 20-181（2014年）的内容，其现行有效性及是否已被后续版本替代，应另行核对；不能把本页内容直接视为当前强制规则。

<summary>
本页依据AC 20-181第2节，说明AHRS辅助源的定义、内部与外部辅助源安装评估，以及GNSS、ADC、皮托管空速和磁辅助的鉴定、性能与告警要求。
</summary>
<content>
# AHRS辅助源

来源文件：AC 20-181《Airworthiness Approval of Attitude Heading Reference System (AHRS) Equipment》，日期原文为 4/7/14；以下整理第2节，原文页码未在给定内容中标明。该文件为咨询通告，不是联邦航空法规（CFR）本身；原文使用“should/ensure”等指导性措辞，以下“应/确保”等表述不等同于强制法规要求。

AC 20-181 第2节将AHRS辅助源定义为：向核心捷联式姿态航向参考功能提供额外传感器信息的内部或外部系统。全球导航卫星系统（GNSS）和大气数据计算机（ADC）辅助源常用于识别飞机加速度，以减少姿态功能中的误差。磁通门和磁力计为航向功能提供磁基准，众多来源可用于性能监控。某些辅助设计仅补充AHRS功能，辅助源丧失可能仅对AHRS性能产生有限影响；在其他设计中，辅助可能提供不可或缺的信息，辅助源丧失可能导致AHRS功能丧失。

## 2.1 内部辅助源安装

应将内部辅助源作为整体产品预期功能评估的一部分进行评估。内部辅助源应作为TSO-C201设计批准过程的一部分进行鉴定。应确保辅助源按预期用途，以适当的精度、完整性、可用性、软件等级和电子硬件设计保证提供所需输入。

例如，如果系统为通用航空飞机开发，但将安装到通勤类飞机上，则内部辅助源可能需要重新评估，以确保与飞机设计架构及其使用方式具有适当的兼容性。

## 2.2 外部辅助源安装

本段适用于未作为TSO-C201产品设计批准的一部分进行鉴定的外部辅助源。

### 2.2.1 外部辅助源性能

当AHRS需要外部辅助源时，应确保安装在飞机上的辅助源提供适当的精度、完整性、可用性、软件等级和电子硬件设计保证。

### 2.2.2 外部辅助源告警

申请人应确定外部辅助源失效和告警如何影响AHRS性能。应视需要进行地面和飞行试验，以确保告警及飞行员动作的适当性。

任何告警应在运行上相关，以尽量减少飞行机组工作负荷；应清晰、明确且及时；应仅在相应状态存在时显示；应始终位于电子显示器的特定区域；当需要飞行机组立即感知时，应位于飞行机组的主视区。

如果无法进行试验，可接受符合性方法是提供分析，以确保外部辅助源降级或失效时采取适当动作。例如，如果AHRS在辅助源失效时禁用姿态输出或切换模式，则作为§§23.1309、25.1309、27.1309或29.1309安全分析的一部分，应确保当辅助源被有意禁用时AHRS按设计动作。

## 2.3 GNSS辅助

GNSS指提供自主地理空间定位的所有类型定位卫星。常见GNSS系统包括但不限于：导航信号定时与测距（NAVSTAR）全球定位系统（GPS）（美国）、全球导航卫星系统（GLONASS）（俄罗斯）和Galileo（欧洲）。GNSS速度数据可用于计算纵向加速度，以帮助消除误差。

### 2.3.1 GNSS鉴定

当将AHRS与外部GNSS接口时，应确保外部GNSS以适当的精度、完整性、可用性以及软件和硬件设计保证提供所需输入。

当与外部GNSS接口时，应确保外部GNSS符合以下任一标准任何修订版的要求：

- TSO-C145d《使用星基增强系统增强的全球定位系统的机载导航传感器》；
- TSO-C146d《使用星基增强系统增强的全球定位系统的独立机载导航设备》；或
- TSO-C196b《使用飞机基增强的全球定位系统设备的机载补充导航传感器》。

本咨询通告不涉及AHRS与TSO-C129a《使用全球定位系统（GPS）的机载补充导航设备》的接口，因为该TSO设计标准在高干扰环境中可能无法提供足够的可用性。

### 2.3.2 GNSS速度精度

如果使用GNSS位置源的速度精度，应确保GNSS源数据满足AHRS安装所规定的最低速度精度要求。GNSS位置源为获得TSO授权，不要求通过速度精度试验。

验证该性能的一种方法是确保GNSS源通过AC 20-138D《定位与导航系统的适航批准》或后续修订版规定的速度精度试验。通常由GNSS源设备制造商完成这些GNSS试验。

### 2.3.3 GNSS故障

某些GNSS产品可能在数据被标记为无效后输出错误的定位和速度数据。应审查GNSS规范以确定是否可能发生该情况；如果AHRS检测到已告警的GNSS故障，AHRS应停止使用错误的GNSS数据。分析可作为符合性方法。

## 2.4 ADC辅助

ADC信息有助于修正姿态俯仰角和坡度角误差。应确保AHRS与外部ADC的接口经过鉴定，例如符合TSO-C106《大气数据计算机》的任何修订版，并以适当的精度、完整性、可用性以及软件和硬件设计保证提供所需输入。

## 2.5 皮托管空速传感器辅助

皮托管数据信息有助于修正由飞机加速度引入的姿态俯仰角和坡度角误差。它可直接与AHRS接口，通常用于低速度和速度变化不复杂的飞机剖面。

当与AHRS接口时，应确保信息来自经认证的飞机源（例如TSO-C16《电加热皮托管和皮托静压管》），并以适当的精度、完整性、可用性以及软件和硬件设计保证提供所需输入。对于更复杂的速度情况，可能需要与ADC接口。另见第5.5节旋翼机考虑。

## 2.6 磁辅助

当与磁传感器接口时，应确保选择其安装位置，以避免来自飞机结构和系统的干扰。对于与已知飞机磁异常相关的干扰，可能需要补偿器，以确保准确的磁航向信息。应确保所有航向仪表在所有可预见的运行条件下连续工作。

# 高磁干扰区域

## 定义与成因（AC 20-181，4/7/14，第5.2节）

高磁干扰区域可由航空母舰、输电线、高架直升机着陆平台、埋设的混凝土钢筋、靠近飞机的地面设备，或无数其他条件引起。

## 磁干扰补偿功能的评估（第5.2.1节）

当 AHRS 安装包含磁通阀或磁强计时，如果 AHRS 安装包含以下用于补偿磁干扰的功能，应评估这些功能：

- **DG 模式**：临时停用磁通阀或磁强计；
- **手动校准模式**：允许飞行员在远离磁干扰的区域手动校准受影响系统；
- **快速校准能力**：磁干扰消失后能够快速校准；或
- **自动切换（automatic reversion）**：对于磁共振成像（MRI）系统和石油钻井平台属于正常着陆区域的安装，可能要求采用自动切换以满足适用安全要求。定时的自由陀螺模式（DG 或类似）可能是可接受的。应确保系统在着陆和初始校准时可用，或允许具有设定航向校准能力的替代短期非随动模式。需要进行地面或飞行试验以评估其运行和性能能力。

## 安装与环境评估（第5.2.2、5.2.3节）

- 应在代表性环境中评估磁通阀或磁强计的安装，以确保磁干扰最小化。
- 适用时，应评估从高磁干扰区域上电、初始校准、起飞和着陆的影响。

## 飞行手册与 POH 说明（第5.2.4、5.2.5节）

- 应确保将快速校准、手动和自动切换模式的说明加入飞行手册或飞行员操作手册（POH）。
- 适用时，应确保将识别潜在磁干扰的说明加入飞行手册或 POH。

## 解析说明

- 本页内容取自 AC 20-181（文件号 AC 20-181，日期 4/7/14）第5.2节；原文的“should/ensure”为咨询通告中的指导性表述，并非联邦航空法规（CFR）本身的强制要求。
- 原文将“定时的自由陀螺模式（DG 或类似）可能是可接受的”列为可接受符合性表述；“自动切换可能被要求”则限于 MRI 系统、石油钻井平台为正常着陆区域等特定安装条件。
- 本页仅整理原文第5.2节关于高磁干扰区域的内容；引用时应核对最新修订状态及适用型号审定基础。

<content>
# AHRS降级模式

来源：AC 20-181（4/7/14）第3节。该文件为咨询通告，不是联邦航空法规本身；原文中的“should”等措辞属于指导或建议符合性表述。

AC 20-181（4/7/14）第3节说明，TSO-C201 允许一种可选降级模式，用于在 AHRS 发生部分失效或失去辅助源时提供基本姿态性能。该模式意在使操作者即使在仪表气象条件（IMC）下也能保持对航空器的正向控制。[[entity/rtca-do-334|RTCA DO-334《固态捷联姿态航向参考系统最低运行性能标准》]]（MOPS）指出，降级模式可支持巡航飞行、爬升、下降、等待和仪表进近；但降级模式可能不适用于自动驾驶运行或某些飞行程序。应在适航审定期间评估降级模式，以确保设计和运行的适用性；AHRS 工作模式和设备性能的具体信息应参考 AHRS 制造商的安装手册。

## 降级模式适用性（第3.1节）

应按照 §§ 23.1301、25.1301、27.1301 或 29.1301 确定降级模式性能对于预期航空器和运行模式是否可接受。

降级模式可用于任何航空器类型，作为主用和备用姿态源；但 TSO-C201 降级模式主要面向较小的低性能航空器，例如 part 23 和“non-appendix B”part 27 航空器，这些航空器通常按单飞行员审定，因而未安装两套主姿态系统。对于仅有一套主姿态系统的航空器，降级模式提供了在主姿态完全丧失时的一种替代方案。

对于按双飞行员运行审定的航空器，当第一套主姿态系统失效或降级时，使用第二套主姿态系统是首选操作方法。不得将降级模式作为减少航空器所需姿态仪表数量的依据。

如果 AHRS 安装手册对降级模式规定了飞行包线或时间限制，应确保将这些限制纳入飞行手册。降级模式用于非正常条件，不应在地面启用，包括初始系统启动期间或发动机启动后。

## 降级模式测试（第3.2节）

AHRS 设备中有两类降级模式触发方式：一类可在飞行中评估，另一类不能。

对于初始 AHRS 安装，如果降级模式可在飞行中禁用（例如拔出断路器），则应通过飞行试验评估降级模式。

对于初始 AHRS 安装，如果降级模式不能在飞行中评估（例如加速度计降级），申请人可使用分析或仿真。测试应包括飞行员工作负荷、降级模式在正常仪表飞行规则（IFR）机动中的可接受性（包括爬升、下降、标准速率转弯和仪表进近）；还应评估对飞行机组在飞行中控制航空器能力的任何影响。

后续安装（follow-on installations）应针对独特的航空器飞行包线或运行条件证明降级模式性能。使用分析来符合 §§23.1309、25.1309、27.1309、29.1309 和 25.1523 以及 part 25 附录 D 的申请人，应确保降级模式能安全执行其预定功能，并且不会显著影响飞行员工作负荷或航空器运行。该分析还应考虑对飞行机组在飞行中控制航空器能力的任何影响。无论采用哪种方式，飞机/旋翼机飞行手册补充（A/RFMS）都应包含降级模式性能特征和限制。

## 其他系统接口（第3.3节）

降级模式性能的定义用于支持主姿态、航向、转弯率和侧滑指示。应评估降级模式性能对其他应用的适用性，因为其对于更高性能应用可能不足，例如自动驾驶、平视显示器（HUD）或合成视景系统（SVS）显示。如果分析表明降级模式对其他航空器应用不足，应确保降级模式不会驱动这些特定航空器应用。

## 操作说明（第3.4节）

应确保适当的 A/RFMS 或适用操作说明更新，加入降级模式描述、降级模式下提供的通告，以及操作航空器的说明。操作说明还应指出将丢失哪些系统应用（例如自动驾驶），以及在降级模式下可完成的机动或运行类型的限制。

本页整理的是 AC 20-181（4/7/14）第3节内容；其现行有效性、是否被后续版本替代，应另行核对，不能直接视为当前强制规则。

| 4 | 降级模式与适用规章、机型类别 | 按 §§23.1301/25.1301/27.1301/29.1301 判定降级模式对预期航空器与运行模式是否可接受；TSO-C201 降级模式主要面向较小低性能航空器（如 part 23 与“non-appendix B”part 27）；不得以此减少所需姿态仪表数量；安装手册的飞行包线或时间限制须纳入飞行手册；不得在地面启用 | <kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="4fed905d-5e4c-4dd1-95de-8dec7d9116b3" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" /><kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="ece7b269-0d76-49be-be89-7f89b29679a9" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" /> |
| 5 | 分类字符串与应用匹配 | 六位类别串（如 A4H4T3）中，首两位为姿态精度、三四位为航向精度与可用性、五六位为转弯与侧滑；不同工作模式可能有不同类别串；HUD、自动驾驶、EFVS、FMS 等应用可能要求更高类别，须与接口系统的姿态/航向性能与适航要求核对 | <kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="9421756e-5bfb-4eee-ba7e-5e4db3f98447" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" /><kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="0ff67505-a594-4b87-b2ea-81af9ee021b8" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" /> |
| 6 | 运行条件 | 极地（地磁异常导致错误磁航向、真航向标识、磁/真航向自动切换告警、飞行手册更新）；低功率/低电压对显示的影响；热带或极地急流 18,000–40,000 ft MSL 与接近失速的低速大顶风；与风切变系统集成时需验证工作能力与限制 | <kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="219981f0-0ff8-49e0-9658-110f74620ec2" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" /><kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="a8712f1a-6f57-4997-abf3-cdd9aa4a2d87" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" /><kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="2e33913b-1778-462b-9890-e0d0dcefba1f" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" /><kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="507765c2-c62c-48d4-aea4-e23f94596b16" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" /> |

**关于“复合材料”的界限**：AC 20-181 的文本只要求“避免机体结构与系统的干扰”“在代表性环境中评估”，未就复合材料机身给出专门判据。因此，铝结构飞机上的数据能否代表复合材料安装的磁环境与结构耦合，不能由该文件直接判定；申请人须另行论证，而不是默认沿用。另可参考 AC 20-180 的提示：某个型号若存在独特且复杂的安装问题（原文举例即“如何在复合材料结构上正确穿孔压力容器”），宜考虑以既有基线数据加补充要求申请新的非 AML 的 STC<kb doc="AC_20-180.pdf" chunk_id="62d1c2dc-c25e-443d-a05e-5c0993328432" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" />。

## 不能仅靠共用基线数据推进的情形

1. **相似性与基线数据无法确立时，AML-STC 就不是适当方法**：AC 20-180 明确“If installation variation between models is such that the similarities and baseline data cannot be established, then AML-STC is not the proper method of approval”<kb doc="AC_20-180.pdf" chunk_id="9259d265-e30d-414a-ad08-7f80edd1da54" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" />。
2. **基线数据必须逐型号确立适用性，且每个型号都要表明符合 §21.20**（型号设计、证实性数据、飞行手册补充），“不是一揽子批准”<kb doc="AC_20-180.pdf" chunk_id="9259d265-e30d-414a-ad08-7f80edd1da54" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" /><kb doc="AC_20-180.pdf" chunk_id="3705aad7-9fcf-4093-9520-acd528861605" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" />。
3. **振动频谱法本身会产生“每一安装专用件号”**，这从根本上否定了单一软件/滤波构型直接套用到新安装<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="74448d33-db11-4170-8962-ef0f25bf76ce" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" />。
4. **需要地面或飞行试验才能确认的项目**：磁干扰补偿功能（DG、人工/快速对准、自动回退）的运行与性能能力<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="2e33913b-1778-462b-9890-e0d0dcefba1f" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" />；外部辅助源失效告警与机组动作的适当性（无法试验时才以分析替代）<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="7b6687b0-fc67-40e8-88b7-0355dadc811e" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" />。
5. **新件极地运行**需飞行试验演示，或证明已在“like or similar installation”的飞机上成功演示；仅 follow-on（后续）安装才可用仿真/分析<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="219981f0-0ff8-49e0-9658-110f74620ec2" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" />。
6. **可在飞行中禁用的降级模式**应通过飞行试验评估；后续安装还须针对独特飞行包线或运行条件演示降级模式性能<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="770bf72f-942a-4298-acfe-264546d3acf9" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" />。
7. **低速皮托/静压数据影响姿态解算**时须演示或评估，并可能施加运行限制<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="74448d33-db11-4170-8962-ef0f25bf76ce" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" />。
8. **直接控制航空器的系统可能不适合 AML-STC**：涉及控制输入的安装（原文以自动驾驶为例）“may require careful design, installation, and testing on each proposed model regardless of baseline data shared between them”；若 AHRS 输出参与自动驾驶或控制回路，这一点尤其要评估<kb doc="AC_20-180.pdf" chunk_id="2441846f-0493-4683-b94c-52cfa4f7b2b2" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" />。
9. **可接受的替代路径**（并非一律重做）：独特风场无法试验时，可由安装方提供分析并写入 A/RFMS 限制<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="507765c2-c62c-48d4-aea4-e23f94596b16" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" />；不可在飞行中评估的降级模式可用分析或仿真，但须覆盖飞行员工作负荷与常规 IFR 机动<kb doc="AC_20-181.pdf" chunk_id="770bf72f-942a-4298-acfe-264546d3acf9" kb_id="17a4fb08-2f1e-4107-b1e6-c203657a3e08" />。

## 无法从现有资料确定的事项

- 具体的**环境鉴定**标准与试验剖面（如 DO-160 类别）在 AC 20-181 的检索内容中没有相应条款；因此，“既有环境鉴定是否足够”不能据该文件得出结论，须以适用的环境鉴定与安装评估资料另行核实。
- 复合材料结构对磁传感器精度、结构耦合与振动传递的**具体量化影响**同样未见条款，不能推断，也不能据此默认可共用或必须重做。

相关背景页可参见 [[concept/rotorcraft-ahrs-installation-vibration-filtering|旋翼机AHRS安装与振动滤波]]、[[concept/ahrs-aiding-sources|AHRS辅助源]]、[[concept/high-magnetic-disturbance-areas|高磁干扰区域]]、[[concept/ahrs-degraded-mode|AHRS降级模式]]、[[concept/aml-stc|AML-STC]]。
